By writing down her feelings and giving them a name, Susie felt better. From then on, anytime she felt dizzy, she remembered the name she had given it and it made her feel better.

The End.

The bird's singing made the home feel even more calm and peaceful. The little bird was happy to be home and to sing its heart out. And from that day on, the bird sang every day in its calm and cozy home.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to draw and write in her journal. One day, she was playing outside when she found a pretty rock. 

Lily: "Look Mommy, I found a rock! Can I mark it with my name?"

Mommy: "Sure Lily, let's get your journal so you can write about it too."

Lily carefully marked her rock with her name and put it in her pocket for safe keeping. She ran back to her house to write about her special find in her journal. 

Lily: "Mommy, my rock is safe in my pocket. I can't wait to write about it in my journal!"

Mommy: "That's great Lily, I can't wait to read all about it." 

Lily happily wrote in her journal about her rock and how she marked it with her name. She felt proud of her special treasure and couldn't wait to show it to her friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys, especially his action figures. He had a Batman figure and a Spiderman figure. 

One day, Timmy's friend Jimmy came over to play. Jimmy wanted to play with Timmy's Spiderman figure, but Timmy didn't want to share. Timmy told Jimmy that he lost the Spiderman figure, but it was a lie. 

Jimmy was sad and went home. Later that day, Timmy's mom found the Spiderman figure under Timmy's bed. She asked Timmy why he lied to Jimmy. Timmy felt bad and said sorry. 

The next day, Timmy went to Jimmy's house to apologize. But Jimmy didn't want to be friends with Timmy anymore. Timmy felt rough inside, but he knew he did something wrong. He learned that lying can hurt people and make them not want to be friends anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a cozy bed with a warm mattress. One day, Lily decided to jump on her bed even though her mom told her not to. Suddenly, the mattress tore and feathers flew everywhere. 

Lily's mom was very upset and told her that she would be punished for not listening. Lily felt sad and knew she had done something wrong. She helped her mom clean up the feathers and promised to never jump on her bed again. 

The next night, Lily snuggled into her warm bed and felt happy knowing she had learned her lesson. She closed her eyes and fell asleep, dreaming of all the fun things she could do without getting into trouble.

The birdie's friends saw what happened and they wanted to give him a reward for being so smart. They gave him some tasty seeds and he was very happy. The birdie knew that he did a good job and felt proud of himself.

The cat felt foolish for not being able to catch the birdie. He realized that he should not have tried to catch the birdie and instead, should have just enjoyed listening to him whistle. From that day on, the cat and the birdie became friends and would sit together and listen to the birdie whistle.

"I found a toy car on the ground, do you want to play with me?" Johnny replied. 

Timmy knew that taking something that didn't belong to him was against the law, but he wanted to play with the toy car so badly that he didn't listen to his conscience. 

After they were finished playing, Timmy felt guilty and went to return the toy car. However, the owner of the toy car saw Timmy and Johnny playing with it and called the police. 

Timmy learned his lesson that it's always important to follow the law and do the right thing.

Later that day, Lily's little brother Jack wanted to play with the pebble. Lily said no because she was afraid he would lose it. Jack got upset and started crying. Lily's mommy came over and asked what was wrong. Jack said he wanted to play with the pebble but Lily wouldn't let him. 

Mommy asked Lily why she wouldn't let Jack play with the pebble. Lily said, "I don't want him to lose it because it's very pretty and I understand how much it means to me." Mommy smiled and told Lily she was very kind to care about her pebble, but it's important to share with others. So, Lily gave the pebble to Jack and they both played with it together.

Just then, a kind man walked by and saw her struggling. "Don't worry, I'll help you release your kite," he said. He climbed up the tree and untangled the string. Mia and Ben were playing in the garden. They liked to look for insects and put them in a jar. Mia was bossy and told Ben what to do. "You find the ants, I find the bees," she said.

Ben did not like ants. They bit him and made him cry. He wanted to find bees too, but Mia said no. "Bees are mine, ants are yours," she said. Ben was sad and angry.

He saw a big bee on a flower. He wanted to catch it and show Mia. He was quiet and careful. He moved his hand slowly to the flower. He was almost there. Then he heard a loud snap.

Mia had seen the bee too. She ran to the flower and snapped her jar over it. She smiled and said, "Ha! I got the bee. You are too slow, Ben."

Ben was very sad and angry. He felt a sting on his hand. He looked and saw an ant. It had bitten him. He cried and dropped his jar. His jar broke and the ants ran away.

Mia saw Ben crying and felt sorry. She said, "I'm sorry, Ben. I was too bossy. Do you want to share the bee?"

Ben nodded and smiled. He said, "Yes, please. And can we find some butterflies too?"

Mia nodded and smiled. She said, "Yes, we can. And I will be nice to you."

They hugged and went to look for butterflies. They were happy and played nicely. They liked insects and each other.

Tom and Lily were playing with their toys in the garden. They had a lot of toys, but their favorite was a big pink pig. The pig could make funny noises and move its legs and tail.

"Let's number the pig's legs," Tom said. He liked to number things and learn new words. He pointed to the pig's front leg and said, "One."

Lily nodded and pointed to the other front leg. "Two," she said.

They moved to the back legs and said, "Three" and "Four." They were very happy and proud of themselves.

But then they heard a loud voice from the house. It was their mom. She sounded serious and angry.

"Tom and Lily, come inside right now! It's time for lunch and you have to wash your hands. And stop playing with that pig. It's dirty and it belongs to the farmer next door. He will be very mad if he sees you with it."

Tom and Lily looked at each other and felt scared. They did not know the pig was not theirs. They thought it was a toy. They quickly put the pig down and ran to the house. They hoped the farmer would not find out and take the pig away. They liked the pig and wanted to play with it again. Maybe they could number its ears and eyes next time.

Anna and Ben were playing in the park. They saw a big yellow dog lying on the grass. The dog looked friendly and sleepy.

"Can we pet the dog?" Anna asked Ben.

"I don't know. Maybe we should ask the owner first," Ben said.

They looked around and saw a man sitting on a bench. He had a book in his hand. He looked smart and kind.

"Excuse me, sir. Is that your dog?" Anna called to him.

The man looked up and smiled. "Yes, that's my dog. His name is Wisdom. He's very gentle and loves children. You can pet him if you want."

"Thank you, sir. Why did you name him Wisdom?" Ben asked.

The man closed his book and walked over to them. He stroked the dog's fur and said, "Because he taught me a lot of things. He taught me how to be patient, loyal, and grateful. He taught me how to enjoy the simple things in life, like lying on the grass and feeling the sun. He taught me how to be a good friend. He's the wisest dog I ever met."

Anna and Ben nodded. They understood. They petted Wisdom and thanked the man. They learned something new that day. They learned that wisdom can come from anyone, even a big yellow dog.

Tim and Mia were playing in the snow. They made a big snowman with a hat and a scarf. They gave him a carrot nose and two rocks for eyes. They were very happy with their snowman.

But then they saw a seal. The seal was lost and cold. He had swum too far from the icy water. He was looking for his family. He was sad and scared.

"Hello, seal," said Tim. "Why are you here? You need to go back to the water. It is too cold for you here."

The seal nodded. He wanted to go back, but he did not know how. He had followed a fish and got lost. He did not see any water or ice. He only saw snow and trees.

"Don't worry, seal," said Mia. "We will help you. We will solve your problem. We will find the water and ice for you. Come with us."

Tim and Mia took the seal by the flippers. They dragged him along the snow. They looked for signs of water and ice. They asked a bird, a squirrel, and a deer. They followed their directions.

Soon they saw a lake. The lake was frozen. There was a hole in the ice. The seal saw the hole. He saw his family. They were waiting for him. They were happy to see him.

"Thank you, Tim and Mia," said the seal. "You are very kind and smart. You solved my problem. You found the water and ice for me. You are my friends."

The seal gave them a hug and a kiss. He slid into the hole. He joined his family. He waved goodbye to Tim and Mia.

Tim and Mia waved back. They were glad they helped the seal. They went back to their snowman. They gave him a smile. They played some more in the snow. They had a fun day.

Lily was a little girl who liked to play with her dolls. She had many dolls, but her favorite was Anna. Anna had long hair, a blue dress and a big smile. Lily loved to brush Anna's hair and make her talk.

One day, Lily noticed that Anna was not smiling. She looked at Anna and saw that her dress was torn and her hair was tangled. Lily felt sad and asked Anna, "What happened to you? Why are you not happy?"

Anna did not answer. She looked weak and tired. Lily tried to hug her, but Anna felt cold and hard. Lily wondered if Anna was sick or hurt. She decided to take her to Mommy.

Lily ran to the kitchen, where Mommy was making lunch. She held Anna in her arms and said, "Mommy, Mommy, please help Anna! She is not smiling and she is weak and cold!"

Mommy looked at Lily and Anna. She saw the torn dress and the tangled hair. She smiled and said, "Don't worry, Lily. Anna is not sick or hurt. She is just a toy. Toys don't feel or talk like we do. They only look like they do."

Lily was confused. She said, "But Mommy, Anna is my friend. She always smiles and talks to me. She is not just a toy. She is real!"

Mommy hugged Lily and said, "I know, Lily. Anna is your friend and you love her. But she is not real like you and me. She is made of plastic and cloth. She can't feel or talk by herself. You make her feel and talk with your imagination. You are very clever and creative, Lily. That's why you have so much fun with Anna."

Lily thought about what Mommy said. She looked at Anna and said, "Is that true, Anna? Are you not real? Do I make you feel and talk?"

Anna did not answer. She still looked weak and cold. Lily felt a little sad, but also a little curious. She said, "Mommy, can you fix Anna? Can you make her dress and hair nice again? Can you make her warm and soft?"

Mommy nodded and said, "Of course, Lily. I can fix Anna. I can sew her dress and comb her hair. I can put her in the sun and make her warm and soft. Then you can play with her again and make her smile and talk."

Lily smiled and said, "Thank you, Mommy. You are the best. I love you and I love Anna."

Mommy smiled and said, "I love you too, Lily. And I love Anna too. She is a very special doll. She is your friend."

Anna picks another leaf and smells it. She likes the smell. She breaks the leaf and rubs it on her hands. She feels cool and happy. "This is mint," she says. "Mommy uses it to make tea. It is good for you."

Tom and Anna decide to pick some mint and take it to Mommy. They fill their net with mint leaves and run to the house. They see Mommy in the kitchen. She is making cookies. The kitchen is tidy and warm.

"Look, Mommy, we have mint for you!" they say and show her their net. Mommy smiles and hugs them. She takes some mint and puts it in a pot of water. She says, "Thank you, Tom and Anna. You are very sweet and helpful. Mint tea is delicious and healthy. Would you like to try some with your cookies?"

Tom and Anna nod and sit at the table. They sip the mint tea and eat the cookies. They like the taste. They feel proud and happy. They love Mommy and the garden.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park. They saw a big hill with a hole in it. They wanted to see what was inside.

"Let's go to the cave!" Tom said.

"OK, but be careful. It might be dark and scary," Lily said.

They ran to the hill and crawled into the hole. It was dark and cold. They saw some rocks and sticks and bugs. They also saw a big ball.

"Look, a ball!" Tom said. He picked it up and threw it to Lily.

Lily caught the ball and threw it back. They played catch for a while. Then Lily threw the ball too hard. It hit the wall of the cave and made a loud noise.

"Oops!" Lily said.

The noise woke up a big bear that was sleeping in the corner. The bear was angry and roared. It got up and ran towards Tom and Lily.

"Run!" Tom said.

They dropped the ball and ran out of the hole. The bear followed them. It was fast and big.

Tom and Lily were scared. They looked for a place to hide. They saw a big tree with a broken branch. They climbed up the tree and sat on the branch.

The bear reached the tree and tried to climb up too. But the branch was broken and weak. It could not hold the bear's weight. The branch snapped and the bear fell down.

"Ouch!" the bear said.

Tom and Lily saw that the bear was hurt. They felt sorry for the bear. They threw some nuts and berries to the bear.

"Sorry, bear. We did not mean to wake you up. Here, have some food," Lily said.

The bear ate the food and felt better. It looked at Tom and Lily and nodded. It was not angry anymore. It went back to the cave and slept.

Tom and Lily climbed down the tree and went back to the park. They learned a lesson. They should not go into caves without asking. They should also be kind to animals. They hugged each other and went home.

"Wow! Look at that!" Tom says.

They clap and cheer. They have just revealed a secret missile. They have made a successful launch. They are the best friends ever.

"Mom, why is the sky so bad?" Tom asks.

"But I don't like lightning. It hurts my eyes and makes me jump," Anna says.

"I know, Anna. But lightning can also be beautiful and powerful. And it helps the plants and the animals grow. Sometimes, lightning can even make a rainbow," Mom says.

Lily and Ben were playing in the forest. They liked to look for bugs and flowers and birds. They saw a big log that was old and brown. They wondered what was inside.

"Let's open it and see," Ben said. He kicked the log with his foot, but it did not move. He kicked harder, but it still did not move.

"Stop, Ben, you are hurting the log," Lily said. She touched the log gently with her hand. She felt something soft and warm. She heard a small sound.

"What is it?" Ben asked. He came closer and looked.

The parrot looked at Lily and said, "Hello, hello! I am stuck, stuck! Help me, help me!"

Lily saw that the parrot had a string around its foot. The string was tied to the branch. The parrot could not fly away.

"Oh, no!" Lily said. "Who did this to you? Don't worry, I will help you!"

Lily reached for the string and tried to untie it. It was hard and tight. She pulled and pulled, but it did not come off.

"Remove, remove!" the parrot said. "Please, remove!"

Lily had an idea. She took out her scissors from her pocket. She always carried them with her to cut paper and make crafts. She carefully cut the string with the scissors. The parrot was free!

"Thank you, thank you!" the parrot said. "You are kind, kind! You are my friend, friend!"

Lily was happy and proud. She had saved the parrot. She gave it a hug and a kiss.

"You are welcome, welcome!" Lily said. "I am glad, glad! You are my friend, friend!"

The parrot flapped its wings and flew to Lily's shoulder. It nuzzled her cheek and said, "I am grateful, grateful! You are the best, best!"

Lily smiled and laughed. She had a new friend. She named it Polly, too. She and Polly played and talked in the park. They had a lot of fun.

Lila and Ben were playing in the backyard. They found a big barrel that was empty. They rolled it to the fence and stood it up.

"Let's make a fort with the barrel," Lila said. "We can hide inside and pretend we are pirates."

"Okay," Ben said. "But how do we get in? The barrel is too high."

Lila had an idea. She saw a big board lying on the grass. She dragged it to the barrel and leaned it against it. She made a ramp.

"Look, Ben," she said. "We can use the board to climb up. The barrel will support the board and we can support each other."

They took turns climbing up the board and sliding into the barrel. They laughed and shouted. They felt unique and brave.

They played until their mom called them for lunch. They climbed out of the barrel and left the board there.

"Maybe we can play again tomorrow," Lila said.

"Maybe," Ben said. "But we have to remember to put the board away. We don't want anyone to trip over it."

They nodded and ran to the house. They were hungry and happy. They had fun with the barrel.

Lily and Anna were best friends. They liked to play with dolls and dress up. One day, Lily got a new bracelet from her mom. It was shiny and pink and had a heart on it. Lily loved her bracelet and showed it to Anna.

"Wow, your bracelet is so pretty!" Anna said. "Can I try it on?"

"Okay, but be careful," Lily said. "It is very special to me."

Anna put the bracelet on her wrist. It was a bit tight, but she liked how it sparkled. She forgot to be careful and ran around the yard with it. She played with the dog, climbed the tree, and swung on the swing. She was having so much fun that she did not notice the bracelet slipping off her wrist.

Lily saw the bracelet on the ground. She ran to pick it up, but it was too late. The dog saw it too and thought it was a toy. He grabbed it with his mouth and ran away. Lily chased after him, but he was too fast.

"Stop, stop, doggy!" Lily cried. "Give me back my bracelet!"

Anna heard Lily and realized what happened. She felt very bad. She had been careless with Lily's bracelet. She ran after Lily and the dog, hoping to help.

"Doggy, please, drop the bracelet!" Anna said. "It is not yours, it is Lily's!"

The dog did not listen. He thought it was a game. He ran to the fence and tried to squeeze through a hole. But the bracelet was too big and got stuck. The dog pulled and pulled, but he could not get free.

Lily and Anna reached the fence. They saw the dog and the bracelet. Lily was angry and sad. She wanted her bracelet back, but she did not want to hurt the dog.

"Doggy, you are a bad dog!" Lily said. "You took my bracelet and broke it!"

Anna felt sorry for Lily and the dog. She had an idea. She found a stick and waved it in front of the dog. The dog liked sticks. He let go of the bracelet and tried to get the stick. Anna threw the stick away and the dog ran after it.

Lily grabbed the bracelet. It was bent and scratched, but it was still hers. She hugged it and thanked Anna.

"Anna, you are a good friend," Lily said. "You helped me get my bracelet back."

Anna smiled and hugged Lily. She was glad that Lily was not mad at her.

"Lily, I am sorry I was careless with your bracelet," Anna said. "I will never do that again."

Lily forgave Anna. She knew that Anna did not mean to lose her bracelet. She still liked her bracelet, even if it was not perfect. She decided to share it with Anna.

"Anna, you can wear my bracelet sometimes," Lily said. "But only if you are careful."

Anna nodded and thanked Lily. They put the bracelet on Anna's wrist and went back to play. They were still best friends.

Mom looked at the feather and smiled. "That is an ancient feather, Tom. It is from a bird that lived a long time ago, when there were no cars or phones or TVs. It is called a dinosaur feather. Do you know what a dinosaur is?"

Lily and Tom shook their heads. They had never heard of dinosaurs before.

"A dinosaur is a big, scary animal that roared and stomped and ate other animals. Some dinosaurs had feathers, like this one. But they are all gone now. They became fossils in the rocks. This feather is very rare and special. It is a part of history. Do you want to learn more about dinosaurs?"

Lily and Tom nodded. They were curious and excited. They wanted to see more dinosaur feathers and fossils. They wanted to hear more stories about the ancient birds.

"Okay, then let's go to the museum," mom said. "They have a lot of dinosaur things there. You can see them and touch them and ask questions. But first, let's mention this feather to the park ranger. Maybe he knows where it came from and how it got here. Maybe he will let you keep it as a souvenir. What do you think?"

Anna and Ben nod and follow mom to the garage. Mom finds some glue and a wheel that looks like the original one. She puts some glue on the wheel and sticks it to the cart. She holds it for a while until it is dry. Then she turns the cart over and says, "There, it is fixed. Good as new."

Anna and Ben are happy and hug mom. They thank her for repairing their cart. They take their cart back to the yard and put their toys and books and snacks in it. They pull it around and laugh and smile. They love their cart. It is their favorite toy.

Tom laughed and said, "Let me try!" He took the yogurt from Lily and ate some too. He also made a funny face and said, "Yuck, this is sour! It hurts my tongue!"

Mom smiled and said, "I'm sorry, kids. I forgot to check the date on the yogurt. It is old and spoiled. You don't have to eat it. Throw it in the trash and I'll give you something else."

Tom and Lily threw the yogurt in the trash and rinsed their mouths with water. Mom gave them some cookies and milk instead. They ate them happily and said, "Thank you, Mom. These are yummy!"

Anna and Ben were twins who liked to play in the forest. They were eager to find new things and have fun. One day, they saw a big mushroom with red spots on it. It looked like a hat.

"Wow, look at that mushroom!" Anna said. "Can we pick it?"

"I don't know," Ben said. "Maybe it is not good to eat. Maybe it is bad."

They went closer to the mushroom and touched it. It felt soft and wet. They smelled it. It smelled like dirt and grass.

"Maybe we can ask Mommy if we can eat it," Anna said. "She knows a lot about food."

"Okay," Ben said. "But how can we take it home? It is too big for our hands."

They looked around and saw a big leaf on the ground. They put the mushroom on the leaf and lifted it together. It was heavy, but they were strong.

They walked back to their house, holding the leaf with the mushroom. They were happy and proud of their find.

When they got home, they saw Mommy in the kitchen. She was making soup for lunch.

"Mommy, Mommy, look what we found!" Anna said.

"A mushroom!" Ben said.

They showed Mommy the mushroom on the leaf. Mommy looked surprised and scared.

"Oh, no, no, no!" Mommy said. "That is a very bad mushroom! It can make you very sick! You must never eat it or touch it!"

She took the leaf with the mushroom and threw it in the trash. She washed Anna and Ben's hands with soap and water. She hugged them and kissed them.

"I'm so glad you are okay," Mommy said. "You are very lucky. God was watching over you. You should pray and thank Him for keeping you safe."

Anna and Ben nodded. They did not understand why the mushroom was bad, but they trusted Mommy. They prayed and thanked God for their Mommy and their life. They ate the soup and forgot about the mushroom. They decided to play with their toys instead.

Lily and Sam were friends who liked to play outside. They had a wagon that they used to carry their toys and books. One day, a new boy named Ben moved in next door. He saw the wagon and wanted to play with it.

"Can I borrow your wagon?" he asked Lily and Sam.

"Sure, you can borrow it, but you have to be nice and share," Lily said.

Sam nodded and smiled. He liked to make new friends.

Ben took the wagon and put his own toys and books in it. He did not share with Lily and Sam. He pulled the wagon around the yard and ignored them. He was ignorant and rude.

Lily and Sam felt sad and angry. They wanted their wagon back.

"Hey, Ben, can we have our wagon back?" Sam asked.

"No, it's mine now. Go away," Ben said.

He pushed Sam and made him fall. Lily ran to help Sam and shouted at Ben.

"That's not fair! You can't keep our wagon! You have to give it back!" she said.

Ben laughed and ran away with the wagon. He did not care about Lily and Sam. He was a bad boy.

Lily and Sam cried and hugged each other. They wished Ben would be nice and return their wagon. They hoped he would learn to be a good friend.

Sara and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big dog. The dog is brown and furry. It has a long tail and sharp teeth.

"Wow, look at the dog!" Sara says. "It is so big and cute. I want to pet it."

"No, Sara, don't!" Ben says. "The dog is bad. It can bite you. Stay away from it."

But Sara does not listen. She runs to the dog and tries to hug it. The dog does not like it. It growls and snaps at Sara. Sara is scared. She cries and runs back to Ben.

"Are you okay, Sara?" Ben asks. He is worried. He sees a red mark on Sara's arm. The dog bit her.

"It hurts, Ben. The dog was bad. It hurt me." Sara says. She is sad and angry.

"I'm sorry, Sara. I told you to stay away from it. Come, let's go to the nurse. She can help you." Ben says. He takes Sara's hand and leads her to the nurse's office.

The nurse is kind. She cleans Sara's wound and puts a band-aid on it. She gives Sara a lollipop and a hug.

"You were brave, Sara. The dog was bad, but you are good. You will be fine." The nurse says.

"Thank you, nurse. You are nice." Sara says. She smiles a little.

Ben smiles too. He is glad Sara is okay. He gives her a kiss on the cheek.

"You are my friend, Sara. I care about you." Ben says.

"You are my friend too, Ben. I love you." Sara says.

They hug and hold hands. They are happy. They have learned a lesson. They will never go near a bad dog again. They will always listen to each other. They will always be friends.

Lily was a furry cat who liked to play and nap in her home. She had a big place with many rooms and toys. She also had a family who loved her and gave her food and cuddles. Lily was happy most of the time, but sometimes she felt worry.

One day, Lily heard a loud noise outside. She looked out the window and saw a big truck. The truck had a big box on it. Lily saw her family put some of their things in the box. She saw her bed, her bowl, her ball and her mouse. Lily did not like this. She did not want to lose her things. She did not want to leave her place. She felt worry.

She ran to her family and meowed. She tried to tell them to stop. She tried to get her things back. But they did not listen. They picked her up and put her in a small cage. They put the cage in the car. They drove away from her place. Lily felt more worry.

She did not know where they were going. She did not like the car. She did not like the cage. She did not like the noise. She felt scared. She meowed louder. She scratched the cage. She wanted to go back to her place.

After a long time, the car stopped. Lily saw a new place. It was different from her old place. It had a different color, a different shape, a different smell. She saw her family take her cage out of the car. They opened the cage and let her out. They smiled and said, "Lily, this is our new home. We moved here because we got a new job. We brought all your things with us. Don't worry, you will like it here. We love you, Lily."

Lily looked around. She saw her bed, her bowl, her ball and her mouse. They were in the new place. She saw some new things too. She saw a big sofa, a big window, a big tree. She felt curious. She sniffed the sofa, the window, the tree. She felt some comfort. She saw her family hug her and pet her. She felt some love. She felt less worry.

She decided to give the new place a chance. She decided to play with her toys, nap on the sofa, look out the window, climb the tree. She decided to be happy. She still missed her old place, but she liked her new place too. She liked her family more. She felt no worry.

Lily loved her pony, Max. He was brown and soft and had a long tail. Lily liked to brush his hair and feed him carrots. Sometimes, she rode on his back and he took her around the farm.

But Max was also stubborn. He did not like to do what Lily said. He wanted to go where he liked and eat what he liked. He did not listen to Lily or her dad. He made Lily angry and sad.

One day, Lily and Max went for a ride. Lily wanted to go to the pond, but Max wanted to go to the apple tree. He pulled and pulled on the rope, and Lily pulled and pulled back. They both shouted.

"Max, stop! You are a bad pony! You have to do what I say!" Lily said.

"Neigh! Neigh! I want apples! You are a mean girl! You have to do what I say!" Max said.

They fought and fought, until they both fell off. Lily hurt her knee and Max hurt his nose. They both cried.

Lily's dad heard them and came to help. He picked up Lily and hugged her. He checked Max and gave him a pat. He said, "Lily, Max, you have to be nice to each other. You are friends, not enemies. You have to share and take turns. Do you remember when you first met?"

Lily and Max nodded. They remembered. Lily remembered how she saw Max in the barn and how he licked her hand. Max remembered how he saw Lily in the field and how she gave him a carrot. They remembered how they played and laughed and cuddled.

They looked at each other and felt sorry. They said, "I'm sorry, Lily/Max. You are a good girl/pony. I like you. Can we be friends again?"

They hugged and kissed and said, "Yes, we can. Let's go to the pond and the apple tree together. We can have fun and be happy."

Lily and Max smiled and got back on. They followed Lily's dad to the pond and the apple tree. They shared the water and the apples. They were nice to each other. They were friends.

Sara and Ben are friends. They like to play outside in the sun. One day, they find a big hill with green grass and yellow flowers. They want to go to the top of the hill.

"Let's skip to the tip!" Sara says. She holds Ben's hand and they start to skip. Skipping is fun. They feel happy and free.

They skip and skip and skip. They see birds and bugs and clouds. They laugh and sing and talk. They are almost at the tip of the hill.

But then, Ben trips on a rock. He falls down and hurts his knee. He cries and cries. He does not want to skip anymore.

Sara stops skipping. She sees Ben is sad and hurt. She runs to him and hugs him. She says, "I'm sorry, Ben. Are you OK?"

Ben sniffles and nods. He shows Sara his knee. It has a small cut and some blood. Sara says, "Don't worry, Ben. It's not bad. I have a band-aid in my pocket. I can put it on your knee. It will make it better."

Sara takes out a band-aid. It has a picture of a star on it. She sticks it on Ben's knee. She says, "There. Now you have a star on your knee. You are brave and strong."

Ben smiles and says, "Thank you, Sara. You are kind and sweet."

Sara says, "You're welcome, Ben. You are my friend. Do you want to skip to the tip again?"

Ben says, "Yes, I do. But can we go slow and careful?"

Sara says, "Of course we can. We can go as slow and careful as you want. We can also stop and rest if you need."

Ben says, "OK. That sounds good. That sounds comfortable."

Sara says, "Yes, it does. It sounds comfortable and fun."

They hold hands again and start to skip. They skip slow and careful. They skip to the tip of the hill. They see the sun and the sky and the world. They feel happy and free. They are friends.

Lily liked to look at the books on the bookcase. She liked the pictures and the colors. She wanted to read the words, but they were too hard. She asked her mom to read to her.

"Mom, can you read me a story?" Lily said.

"Sure, honey. Which one do you want?" Mom said.

Lily pointed to a book with a princess on the cover. She liked princesses. They had pretty dresses and crowns.

Mom took the book and opened it. She read to Lily about the princess who lived in a big castle. She was very rich and had many things. But she was not happy. She wanted to have friends and play outside.

Lily listened to the story. She felt sorry for the princess. She did not want to be rich and lonely. She wanted to have fun and laugh.

"Mom, can the princess change?" Lily asked.

"What do you mean, change?" Mom said.

"Can she be like me? Can she go to the park and play with other kids? Can she wear jeans and sneakers?" Lily said.

Mom smiled. She hugged Lily and said, "Yes, she can. The princess can change if she wants to. She can choose to be happy and free. She can make her own story."

Lily smiled too. She liked that idea. She said, "Mom, can we make our own story?"

"Of course, we can. We can do anything we want. We have each other and we have books. We are rich in our own way." Mom said.

They closed the book and put it back on the bookcase. They got up and went to the park. They played and laughed. They made their own story.

Ben and Mia were very tired. They had played all day with their toys, their books and their dog. They had eaten a lot of bread and butter for dinner. Now it was time to go to bed.

But Ben and Mia did not want to go to bed. They wanted to stay up and watch TV with their mom and dad. They said, "Please, please, can we watch TV? Just a little bit?"

Mom and dad shook their heads. They said, "No, no, you have to go to bed. TV is not good for you at night. It will make your eyes hurt and your dreams bad. You need to sleep and rest."

Ben and Mia pouted. They said, "But TV is so fun and interesting. We want to see the animals and the cars and the people. We want to learn new things."

Mom and dad smiled. They said, "You can learn new things tomorrow. There are many books and games and puzzles that you can play with. TV is not the only way to learn. And TV is very expensive. We have to pay a lot of money to watch it. We have to save money for other things, like food and clothes and toys."

Ben and Mia yawned. They were starting to feel sleepy. They said, "OK, OK, we will go to bed. But can you read us a story first? A story about animals and cars and people?"

Mom and dad nodded. They said, "Of course, we can read you a story. A story that is fun and interesting and not expensive. Come on, let's go to your room and pick a book."

Ben and Mia hugged their mom and dad. They said, "Thank you, thank you, you are the best. We love you very much."

Mom and dad hugged them back. They said, "We love you too. You are our precious children. Now let's go to bed and have sweet dreams."

Lily and Tom were playing in the park. They liked to slide, swing and run. They saw a big tree with many leaves. They wanted to hide under the tree and pretend they were animals.

They ran to the tree and crawled under the leaves. They made noises like lions, monkeys and birds. They had fun.

But then they heard a loud laugh. It was a witch! She had a long nose, a black hat and a broom. She saw Lily and Tom under the tree. She wanted to catch them and make them her pets.

"Ha ha ha, I found you, little ones!" the witch said. "Come out, come out, or I will shake the tree and make you fall!"

Lily and Tom were scared. They did not want to be the witch's pets. They wanted to run away. But they did not know how to get out of the tree.

They whispered to each other. "What can we do?" Lily asked. "We have to be quiet and smart," Tom said.

They looked around and saw a big stick. They had an idea. They grabbed the stick and waited for the witch to come closer.

When the witch reached the tree, she smiled. She thought she had them. She grabbed the broom and started to shake the tree.

But Lily and Tom were ready. They used the stick to poke the witch in the nose. The witch screamed and dropped the broom. Lily and Tom jumped out of the tree and ran to the broom. They climbed on the broom and flew away.

"Bye bye, witch!" they shouted. "You can't catch us!"

The witch was angry and sad. She rubbed her nose and cried. She had lost her broom and her pets.

Lily and Tom were happy and brave. They flew to their home and told their mom and dad what happened. They hugged them and said they loved them.

They never played under the tree again.

Lily wanted a haircut. She had long hair that got in her eyes and mouth. She asked her mom to take her to the salon. Her mom said yes, but they had to wait for her dad to come home.

Lily was impatient. She saw scissors on the table. She thought she could cut her own hair. She took the scissors and went to the bathroom. She looked in the mirror and started to snip snip snip.

Her mom heard the noise and ran to the bathroom. She saw Lily with a mess of hair on the floor and on her head. She was shocked and angry. She said, "Lily, what did you do? You ruined your hair! You were selfish and did not wait for me. Now we have to buy a new haircut for you and it will cost a lot of money."

Lily felt sorry. She did not mean to make her mom mad. She said, "I'm sorry, mom. I wanted a haircut. I thought I could do it myself. I did not know it was hard. Please don't be mad at me."

Her mom hugged her and said, "I'm not mad at you, Lily. I love you. But you have to be careful with scissors. They are sharp and dangerous. And you have to listen to me. I know what is best for you. Come on, let's go to the salon and fix your hair. Maybe you can choose a nice color or a ribbon to make it look pretty."

Anna and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. They liked to pretend they were in a different world, where they could do anything they wanted. They had a big box that they used as a door to their world.

"Let's enter our world and have some fun!" Ben said. He picked up his toy sword and his hat. "I'm a brave knight, and you're a princess."

Anna nodded and grabbed her doll and her crown. "I'm a princess, and you're my knight. Let's go!" She followed Ben to the box and crawled inside.

Inside the box, they saw a lot of colorful pictures that they had drawn and stuck on the walls. They had a castle, a forest, a dragon, and a treasure. They smiled and started to play.

But then, they heard a loud noise outside the box. It was their big brother, Tom. He was angry because he wanted to watch TV, and they were making too much noise.

"Hey, you two, get out of my way!" Tom shouted. He kicked the box and made it fall over. Anna and Ben screamed and fell out of the box. Their toys and pictures were scattered on the floor.

"Tom, you're mean!" Anna cried. She hugged her doll and her crown.

"Tom, you're bad!" Ben yelled. He waved his sword and his hat.

Tom laughed and walked to the TV. He turned it on and ignored them.

Anna and Ben were sad and angry. They looked at their ruined world and felt like crying. But then, they had an idea. They got up and ran to their room. They took another box and some more paper and crayons. They decided to make a new world, where Tom could not enter. They worked hard and made it even better than before. They smiled and crawled inside.

"Let's enter our world and have some fun!" Anna said. She picked up her doll and her crown. "I'm a princess, and you're my knight."

"Let's go!" Ben said. He picked up his sword and his hat. "I'm a brave knight, and you're a princess."

They played happily in their new world, and forgot about Tom and his TV. They had each other, and that was enough.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play with their toys. They had a big tree in their living room with many shiny things on it. They were called ornaments and they were very pretty. Lily and Ben wanted to touch them, but Mommy said no. She said they were breakable and not for playing.

One night, Lily and Ben woke up when it was dark. They heard a noise from the living room. They got out of their beds and tiptoed to the door. They opened it and saw a big man in a red suit. He had a big bag on his back and he was putting things under the tree. He was Santa!

Lily and Ben were very excited. They wanted to say hello to Santa and see what he brought them. They ran to the living room and shouted, "Santa, Santa, we are here!"

Santa turned around and smiled. He said, "Ho ho ho, hello Lily and Ben. You are very brave and tough to wake up and see me. But you should be sleeping, it is not time to open your gifts yet."

Lily and Ben looked at the tree and saw many boxes with ribbons and bows. They also saw some new ornaments that Santa had hung on the tree. They were very curious and wanted to touch them.

Santa said, "Be careful, these ornaments are very special. They are from different places in the world. They tell stories and make wishes. But they are also very fragile and can break easily. You have to be gentle and respectful with them."

Lily and Ben nodded. They reached for the ornaments and touched them softly. They felt warm and sparkly. They heard some sounds and saw some pictures in their minds. They saw snow and mountains and animals and people. They felt happy and amazed.

Santa said, "Do you like them? They are my gift to you. They will help you learn and dream and grow. But you have to promise me something. You have to promise to take good care of them and share them with each other. Can you do that?"

Lily and Ben said, "Yes, Santa, we promise. Thank you, thank you, thank you!"

Santa said, "You are very welcome, Lily and Ben. You are very good and sweet children. Now, you have to go back to your beds and sleep. I have to go to other houses and deliver more gifts. I will see you next year. Merry Christmas!"

Lily and Ben hugged Santa and said, "Merry Christmas, Santa! We love you!"

Santa hugged them back and said, "I love you too, Lily and Ben. Good night!"

Lily and Ben ran back to their beds and snuggled under their blankets. They closed their eyes and smiled. They had the best night ever. They had met Santa and he had given them the most wonderful ornaments. They could not wait to wake up and see them again.

Lila and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big cage. Inside the cage, there is a lion. The lion is sleeping.

"Wow, look at the lion!" Tom says. "He is so big and strong. I want to meet him."

"No, Tom, that is a bad idea," Lila says. "The lion is not a friend. He is wild and dangerous. He can bite you and hurt you. We should stay away from the cage."

But Tom does not listen to Lila. He is foolish. He thinks he is brave and smart. He climbs over the fence and goes near the cage. He tries to wake up the lion.

"Hello, lion, I am Tom. Do you want to play with me?" he says.

The lion opens his eyes. He sees Tom. He is angry and hungry. He roars loudly and shows his big teeth. He tries to break the cage and catch Tom.

Tom is scared. He realizes he made a mistake. He runs back to the fence and climbs over it. He joins Lila, who is waiting for him.

"Tom, you are so foolish!" Lila says. "You could have been eaten by the lion. You are lucky he was in the cage. You should never do that again. You should listen to me and be careful."

Lily and Max were playing in the park. They liked to swing on the swings and slide on the slide. They saw a big dog with a chain around its neck. The dog was barking and pulling on the chain. It looked angry and scary.

"Let's go see the dog!" Max said. He ran towards the dog.

"No, Max, stop!" Lily said. She was scared of the dog. She ran after Max and grabbed his hand. "The dog might bite you. We need to stay away."

"But I want to pet the dog. He looks lonely," Max said. He tried to pull his hand away from Lily.

Lily was thoughtful. She knew Max liked animals. She also knew the dog was not happy. She had an idea. She pointed to a nearby bench. "Look, Max. There is a man sitting on the bench. He has a chain too. Maybe he is the dog's owner. Maybe he can help us."

"Excuse me, sir," Lily said. "Is that your dog?"

The man looked up from his book. He saw the dog and the children. He smiled. "Yes, that's my dog. His name is Rex. He is very friendly, but he gets excited when he sees new people. He doesn't mean to be scary. He just wants to play."

"Can we play with him?" Max asked.

"Sure, if you want to. But you have to be careful. He is very strong and he might knock you down. And you have to ask him first. You have to let him sniff your hand and then pet him gently. Do you want to try?"

Max and Lily nodded. They followed the man to the dog. The man held the chain and told the dog to sit. The dog obeyed. He stopped barking and wagged his tail. He sniffed Max and Lily's hands and licked them. He let them pet him and scratch his ears. He was soft and warm.

Ben was scared. He wanted to stop, but he did not know how. He asked, "How can I make you go away?" The spirit said, "You can't. I will stay with you forever. You are mine." Ben cried. He wished he never asked the light in his closet. He wished he listened to his mom, his dad, his sister, and his teacher. He wished he had a good friend, not a bad spirit. But it was too late. The spirit laughed. He said, "You asked for it."

Tom and Lily liked to play near the lake. They saw a fisherman with a big hat and a long stick. He threw a string into the water and waited.

"Can we watch him?" Lily asked Tom.

"OK, but we have to be quiet," Tom said. "He is trying to catch fish."

They sat on the grass and looked at the fisherman. He was very alert. He watched the string and felt the stick. Sometimes he smiled and sometimes he frowned.

"What is he doing?" Lily whispered.

"He is guessing," Tom whispered back. "He is guessing if there is a fish on the string or not. If there is, he will pull the stick and get the fish. If not, he will throw the string again."

They watched for a long time. The fisherman guessed right and wrong many times. He caught some fish and put them in a basket. He missed some fish and shook his head.

"Wow, he is good at guessing," Lily said.

"Yes, he is," Tom agreed. "But I think we are better at guessing."

"How?" Lily asked.

"Let's guess how many fish he has in his basket," Tom said. "I guess five."

"I guess six," Lily said.

They got up and walked to the fisherman. They smiled and said hello.

"Hello, kids," the fisherman said. "Do you like fishing?"

"Yes, we do," Tom and Lily said.

"We were watching you," Tom said. "You are very good at guessing."

"Thank you," the fisherman said. "But how do you know that?"

"We were guessing too," Lily said. "We were guessing how many fish you have in your basket."

"Really?" the fisherman said. "And how many do you think I have?"

Tom and Lily said their guesses. The fisherman laughed and opened his basket.

"Let's see," he said. "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven. I have seven fish. You are both very close, but Lily is closer. She guessed six."

"Yay, I win!" Lily said.

"Good job, Lily," Tom said.

The fisherman gave them each a fish to take home. They thanked him and said goodbye. They ran back to their house, happy and proud. They had fun guessing with the fisherman.

Lily went to her mom and said, "My friends are speaking a stupid language I don't know." Her mom replied, "Lily, it's not nice to call something stupid just because you don't understand it. Maybe you can ask your friends to teach you."

Lily went back to her friends and asked them to teach her their language. They were happy to help and taught her some new words. Lily felt happy and included again. From then on, she knew that it's important to try and learn new things instead of calling them stupid.

The moral of the story is that we should always try to learn new things and be open to different languages and cultures.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play with her toys. One day, she was playing with her dolls when her mom came into the room.

"Hi Lily, what are you doing?" her mom asked.

"I'm playing with my dolls. Look, they're so flexible!" Lily said, showing her mom how she could move their arms and legs.

"That's great, Lily. Did you know that we can measure how flexible a human is?" her mom said.

"What's measure?" Lily asked.

"Measure means to find out how big or small something is. We can measure how tall or short someone is, or how flexible they are," her mom explained.

"Oh, I see. Can you measure how flexible I am?" Lily asked.

"Sure, let's try it out!" her mom said, and they spent the rest of the afternoon measuring how flexible Lily was.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to hear stories from her grandma. One day, she went to her grandma's house and said, "Grandma, I want a story please." 

Her grandma smiled and said, "Of course, my dear. I have a harmless story about a little bunny who wanted to make new friends." 

Lily was excited and asked, "What did the bunny do, grandma?" 

Her grandma replied, "The bunny went to the forest and met a friendly squirrel and a kind deer. They played together and had lots of fun. The bunny was very happy to have new friends." 

Lily smiled and said, "That's a lovely story, grandma. Thank you for telling me." And with a big hug, she went home, dreaming of her own adventure in the forest with new friends.

"No, I want bananas," replied Max.

"But you've already had so many today. You should eat something else," suggested Lily.

Max didn't listen and kept whining for bananas. Suddenly, Lily had an idea. She took a piece of paper and started to fold it. Max watched curiously.

"What are you doing?" asked Max.

Max was amazed and forgot all about his craving for bananas. He and Lily played together happily, and Max learned that sometimes it's fun to try new things instead of always wanting the same old thing.

On the day of the party, Lily and Tim dressed up their toys. The icy blue car had a shiny hat, and the one-legged doll had a pretty dress. All the friends and toys gathered around. Lily and Tim said, "Now our toys are married!" Everyone clapped and cheered. The toys were happy, and Lily and Tim were best friends forever.

Baby Bird told Mommy Bird about the cat. Mommy Bird became alert. She thought of a plan to save them. She told Baby Bird, "Bow to the cat and be nice. Maybe the cat will not eat us if we are nice."

At the end of the tunnel, Ben found a big, shiny rock. He knew it was special. Ben took the rock home to show his friends. They all thought Ben was the most gifted bunny in the forest.

Tim picked up the piece of paper and looked at it. It had a picture of a treasure chest on it. Tim was excited and showed the paper to his friend, Sam. "Look, I found a treasure map!" said Tim. Sam looked at the map and smiled. "Let's find the treasure!" said Sam.

Tim and Sam followed the map. They walked and walked until they found a big rock. Behind the rock, they discovered a small box. They opened the box and found shiny, pretty stones inside. Tim and Sam were so happy. They took the stones home and showed them to their families. Everyone loved the stones and the story of how Tim and Sam found the treasure.

In the end, Tim and Sam became best friends. The moral of the story is that being patient and kind can help change an angry heart.

Once upon a time, there was a little pencil who lived in a big box. The pencil was very sad because it was small and helpless. It wanted to stand up tall like the other pencils, but it just couldn't.

One day, a kind crayon saw the sad pencil and asked, "Why are you so sad?" The pencil replied, "I want to stand up tall like the other pencils, but I can't." The crayon thought for a moment and said, "I have an idea! Let's ask the ruler for help."

The crayon and the pencil went to the ruler, who was very wise. The ruler listened to their story and said, "I can help you stand tall, little pencil." The ruler then stood behind the pencil and helped it stand up straight.

The pencil was so happy that it could finally stand tall like the other pencils. It thanked the crayon and the ruler for their help. From that day on, the pencil, crayon, and ruler were the best of friends, always helping each other when they needed it.

The gorilla learned his lesson and promised to be careful with the spray. From then on, he only used it when he needed to. And his friends were happy that he was safe and healthy. The end.

Sarah thought that was really cool. As they continued to drive, they saw a friend of Sarah's playing outside. Sarah said, "Mommy, can we stop and say hi?" Her mom said yes and they pulled over. 

Sarah was so glad to see her friend and they played together for a little while. Then, it was time to go home. Sarah said, "Thank you for the drive, Mommy. I had fun!"

Lily smiled and said, "That was hard work, but we did it! We helped the whale!" Her mom hugged her and said, "Yes, we did. And we made a new friend too."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she went outside to play in the garden. She saw a worm crawling on the ground. Lily picked up the worm and said, "Hello little worm, how are you?"

The worm replied, "I'm not feeling normal today. I think I'm sick." 

Lily felt sad for the worm and said, "Please don't be sad, I will take care of you." 

Lily took the worm inside and put it in a jar with some dirt. She gave the worm some food and water. After a few days, the worm started to feel better. 

One day, Lily went back to the garden to play. She saw some other kids playing with a ball. She wanted to join in, but the other kids said, "No, you can't play with us." 

Lily felt sad and went back inside. She looked at the worm and said, "I'm glad I have you as my friend. You always make me feel better." 

The worm replied, "I'm glad to be your friend too." 

From that day on, Lily and the worm were the best of friends and they always played together.

Once upon a time, there was a wise old owl named Hootie. He lived in a big tree in the forest. One day, a little bird named Tweety came to visit him. 

"Hello, Hootie!" said Tweety. "Do you have any wisdom to share with me today?"

"Yes, little Tweety," said Hootie. "Always remove yourself from danger. That is the wisest thing you can do."

Tweety thanked Hootie and flew away. Later that day, Tweety saw a big snake in the forest. Remembering Hootie's wisdom, Tweety quickly removed himself from danger. 

But sadly, Tweety's friend, another little bird, did not remember Hootie's advice. She flew too close to the snake and the snake ate her. Tweety was very sad and learned that sometimes, even when you remove yourself from danger, bad things can happen.

The nurse smiled and waved goodbye as the bunny hopped back home. From that day on, the nurse never forgot the bunny's scared little voice in the dark forest.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Alice. She was three years old and loved to wander. Every single day she would wander in the forest, exploring and finding new places to discover.

Suddenly, an old woman came up to Alice, with a look of compassion on her face. She told Alice that she knew a way of getting the pole down - if Alice wanted to learn how. 
Alice quickly agreed and the old woman showed her how to use her feet and hands to climb up the pole. 

Alice was so excited, she cheered with joy! She reached the top of the pole and grabbed the treat she had been eyeing. 

The old woman smiled at Alice, her compassionate heart glad that she had helped the wandering little girl achieve her goal. Alice thanked the old woman and wandered on her way, feeling happy that she had made a new friend.

"Because it does not belong to us," explained Tim. "If we take it, that means we are taking something that is not ours."

Jack thought about this and then looked around. He saw a broom, so he used it to clean the leaves off the ground. 

Eventually, Jack noticed a soft, fuzzy peach laying on the ground. "It's okay to take this one," Jack said with a grin.

But before they could take it, out of the corner of his eye, Jack spotted a friendly little bird. The bird flew down and picked up the peach in its beak.

Jack and Tim were sad, but they knew it was the right thing to do. They watched the little bird fly away, carrying the soft and juicy peach.

Once upon a time, there lived an old beetle. He lived up in a tree and talked to the other animals living in the nearby forest. One day, he passed by a young butterfly fluttering around a nearby bush.

The beetle was taken aback and disagreed. He said, "You can't become lucky until you work for it. You need to learn to trust yourself and try new things."

He chopped down the tree. Then he used the wood and branches to help the animals who lived nearby. They all thanked the large bear for his help.

The tree was so glad they found the axe. Now all the animals had homes, food, and shelter. The tree was very proud of the bear and his large axe!

Soon, the flea's nervous energy was broken by a voice. 'Flea', said the voice, 'Come out and speak to me.' Clawing his way out of his hiding place, the flea stepped out and began to speak.

The flea spoke about his life, and how he was scared for what lay ahead. As he spoke, his dread only grew. Then he heard a voice from the corner of the room, 'Don't be scared flea, I'm here to save you!'

The flea's eyes widened in amazement. There standing in the corner, was his best friend, the frog! His best friend had come to save him, to help him out of this nerve wracking situation.

The flea hugged the frog thankful that he was there. He was no longer scared and knew that things would work out. He thanked the frog for coming to his rescue, relieved that he was safe.

The moral of the story: Always play safe and use your hose responsibly.

When Bob woke up the next morning, he thought carefully about his dream. He decided to take some time off and give his body some rest. That day, he stayed in his nest, eating some warm honey and getting some sleep.

The next day Bob felt better and flew again to the trees. He remembered the skull's advice and every day he would take a rest and take care of his body. 
Bob found out that having a healthy body was much more important than flying around the world. He had learnt an important lesson, and he wanted to spread it to the other birds. 

This story teaches us that it is important for us to look after our bodies and take a break when we are feeling unwell or frustrated. So let's take care of ourselves!

He was lucky. A big kangaroo heard him. He was the leader of the kangaroo family. He was strong and brave. He jumped to the baby kangaroo and picked him up. He put him in his pouch and ran away from the bad men.

The bad men were angry. They followed the big kangaroo. They wanted to catch him too. But the big kangaroo was too fast and smart. He dodged the truck and led it to a cliff. He jumped over the cliff and landed on the other side. The truck could not follow him. It stopped at the edge and honked.

The big kangaroo and the baby kangaroo were safe. They went back to the forest. There, they met the baby kangaroo's mom and dad. They were very happy to see him. They hugged him and thanked the big kangaroo. The big kangaroo smiled and said, "You are welcome. We are all kangaroos. We are a family. We unite and help each other."

Tim and Sam were friends who liked to play in the garden. One day, they saw a big, old bean plant that had many green beans on it. They wanted to pick some beans and eat them.

"Look, Sam, beans!" Tim said. "Let's get some."

"OK, Tim, but we have to be careful. This is not our bean plant. It belongs to Mrs. Lee, the old lady who lives next door. She might get angry if we take her beans," Sam said.

But Tim did not listen to Sam. He ran to the bean plant and started to pull some beans. Sam followed him, but he felt scared.

"Tim, stop! We should not do this. It is not nice to take things that are not ours. Mrs. Lee works hard to grow her beans. She might need them for her food," Sam said.

But Tim did not stop. He pulled more and more beans, until he had a big pile of them. He laughed and said, "Look, Sam, we have so many beans! We can eat them all. Who cares about Mrs. Lee? She is old and mean. She never smiles or talks to us."

Sam felt sad and sorry for Mrs. Lee. He did not want to eat the beans. He wanted to put them back. But before he could say anything, he heard a loud voice.

"Hey, you two! What are you doing with my beans?" It was Mrs. Lee. She had seen them from her window. She came out of her house and walked to the bean plant. She looked angry and sad.

Tim and Sam were scared. They dropped the beans and tried to run away. But Mrs. Lee was faster. She caught them and said, "You naughty boys! How dare you steal my beans? Do you know how much I love my beans? They are my only joy in life. I have no family or friends. I grow my beans with care and water them every day. They make me happy and healthy. And you just came and took them without asking. How would you feel if someone did that to you?"

Tim and Sam felt ashamed and sorry. They realized they had done a very bad thing. They looked at Mrs. Lee and said, "We are sorry, Mrs. Lee. We were wrong. We did not think about how you feel. We were selfish and greedy. Please forgive us. We will not do it again. We will help you put the beans back and water them. We will also be your friends and talk to you. You are not old and mean. You are kind and good."

Mrs. Lee smiled and said, "Thank you, boys. I appreciate your apology and your offer. I forgive you. You are not naughty and bad. You are young and curious. You made a mistake, but you learned from it. You can be my friends and help me with my beans. You can also have some beans to eat, but only if you ask me first. And I will also smile and talk to you more. You are not strangers. You are my neighbors."

Tim and Sam smiled and said, "Thank you, Mrs. Lee. We are happy to be your friends and neighbors. We will respect you and your beans. We will also share and care for others. We learned a valuable lesson today."

The end.

Moral value: The story teaches the moral value of respecting other people's property and feelings, as well as the value of apologizing, forgiving, and making friends.

"What's wrong, Tom?" Lily asked, looking at him.

"I have to sneeze!" Tom said, letting go of his nose.

"Then sneeze!" Lily said, moving away from him.

"Ah... ah... ah... CHOO!" Tom sneezed, spraying saliva and snot all over his lion and Lily's giraffe.

"Ew!" Lily said, covering her mouth. "That's disgusting, Tom!"

"I'm sorry, Lily!" Tom said, wiping his nose. "I didn't mean to!"

Lily looked at her giraffe, which was wet and sticky. She felt angry and sad. She loved her giraffe and she didn't want it to be dirty.

"No, I didn't!" Tom said, picking up his lion. "It's just a little sneeze. It will dry soon."

"I don't care!" Lily said, snatching her giraffe from him. "You are a bad friend, Tom! I don't want to play with you anymore!"

Tom and Lily are sad. They say, "Give us back our toys! They are ours! They are not yours!" Sam does not listen. He says, "No, they are mine now. I like them. You are too small to play with them."

Tom and Lily are angry. They try to get their toys back. But Sam is too tall. He holds them high. Tom and Lily cannot reach them. They cry.

A teacher sees them. She comes to help. She says, "Sam, what are you doing? Why are you taking their toys? That is not nice. You have to share. You have to ask. You have to mind their feelings."

Sam feels bad. He says, "I'm sorry. I just wanted to play. I don't have any toys. Can I play with you?" Tom and Lily stop crying. They say, "Yes, you can play with us. But you have to be kind. You have to give us back our toys. They are ours. You can borrow them."

Sam gives them back their toys. He says, "Thank you. I'm sorry. Can I play with your red car, Tom? Can I play with your blue doll, Lily?" Tom and Lily say, "Yes, you can. But you have to be careful. You have to mind our toys."

They all play together. They share their toys and have fun. They are friends.

Ben and Sam were brothers who liked to play with their toys. Ben had a drum that he liked to bang very loud. Sam had a ball that he liked to throw and catch. One day, their mom said she had to go to the shop and she would be back soon. She told them to be good and not make a mess.

Ben and Sam said, "Okay, mom, we will be good." But as soon as mom left, they started to fight. Ben wanted to play with the drum and the ball, but Sam did not want to share. Sam said, "No, Ben, the ball is mine. You have the drum. Go away!" Ben said, "No, Sam, I want both. Give me the ball or I will hit you with the drum!" Sam said, "No, Ben, you are mean. Leave me alone!"

They pushed and pulled and shouted and cried. They did not hear the door open and close. They did not see mom come back with a cake. Mom had bought a cake to serve them as a surprise. She wanted to make them happy. But when she saw them fighting and the toys broken and the room a mess, she was very angry and sad. She said, "Ben and Sam, what have you done? You are very naughty and selfish. You do not deserve the cake. You have to go to your rooms and think about what you did. No cake for you today!"

Ben and Sam stopped fighting and looked at mom. They saw the cake and felt sorry. They said, "Mom, we are sorry. We did not mean to fight. We love you and the cake. Please, can we have some?" But mom said, "No, Ben and Sam, you cannot have some. You have to learn to share and be kind. Maybe tomorrow, if you are good, I will serve you some cake. But not today. Today, you have to go to your rooms and stay there until dinner."

Ben and Sam went to their rooms and cried. They wished they had not fought. They wished they had shared the drum and the ball. They wished they had been good. They could smell the cake from their rooms. It smelled very good. But they could not have any. They felt very bad. They heard mom sing a song in the kitchen. It sounded very distant. They felt very alone.

Tom and Sam were brothers. They liked to play outside in the grass. One day, they saw a green cricket on a leaf. Tom wanted to catch it and put it in a jar. Sam said no, that was mean. The cricket was happy on the leaf.

Tom did not listen to Sam. He ignored him and ran to the leaf. He grabbed the cricket and put it in a jar. He was happy. He showed it to Sam and said, look what I have. Sam was sad. He said, let it go, Tom. The cricket is scared and sad.

Tom did not listen to Sam. He ignored him and took the jar to his room. He put it on his shelf and went to bed. He forgot to make holes in the lid. The cricket could not breathe. It tried to chirp, but no one heard it. It died in the jar.

The next day, Tom woke up and looked at the jar. He saw the cricket was not moving. He shook the jar, but the cricket did not wake up. He realized he had killed it. He felt bad. He wished he had listened to Sam. He cried and said, I'm sorry, cricket. But it was too late. The cricket was gone.

Tom and Amy were playing in the park on Sunday. They liked to swing, slide and run. They saw a big ball near the fence. Tom wanted to kick it hard.

"Let me strike the ball, Amy!" Tom said.

"No, Tom, it is not our ball. Someone else left it here. Maybe they will come back for it," Amy said.

Tom did not listen. He ran to the ball and struck it with his foot. The ball flew over the fence and hit a window. They heard a loud crash and a shout.

"Who did that? Who broke my window?" a voice said.

Tom and Amy were scared. They ran away from the fence and hid behind a tree. They hoped no one would find them.

A man came out of the house with the broken window. He looked angry. He saw the ball on the ground and picked it up. He walked around the park, looking for the children who struck the ball.

He saw Tom and Amy behind the tree. They trembled and held each other.

"Did you do this?" the man asked, pointing at the ball and the window.

Tom and Amy nodded. They were sorry.

"Please don't be mad, mister. We didn't mean to break your window. We were just playing," Amy said.

The man sighed. He saw that they were young and afraid. He decided to be gentle with them.

"It's okay, kids. I know you didn't do it on purpose. But you have to be careful with other people's things. You could have hurt someone or yourself. Next time, ask before you strike a ball that is not yours, okay?" the man said.

Tom and Amy nodded again. They thanked the man and apologized. The man smiled and gave them the ball.

"Here, you can have this ball. But play with it in a safe place, alright? And have fun," the man said.

Tom and Amy were happy. They hugged the man and said goodbye. They took the ball and went to another part of the park. They played with the ball, but they were gentle and careful. They learned their lesson.

But then they hear a loud noise. It is a fire alarm. The librarian says, "Everyone, please go outside. There is a fire in the kitchen. Do not panic. Follow me."

Sara and Ben are scared. They drop their books and toys and hold hands. They follow the librarian and the other people outside. They see smoke and fire trucks and firefighters. They are cold and sad.

But then they see their moms. Their moms hug them and say, "We are so glad you are safe. We are sorry you had to leave the library. But we have a surprise for you. We brought you some cookies and milk. Do you want some?"

Lily liked to play with her toys in her room. She had many toys, but her favorite was a doll with a pink dress and long hair. She named her doll Anna. Lily and Anna did everything together. They read books, had tea parties, and sang songs.

One day, Lily saw a lamp on her mom's desk. The lamp was shiny and had a pretty shade. Lily wanted to see how the lamp worked. She took Anna and went to the desk. She turned the lamp on and off. She liked how the lamp made light.

Lily had an idea. She wanted to make Anna look like a fairy. She thought the lamp shade would fit on Anna's head like a hat. She lifted the lamp shade and put it on Anna. But the lamp shade was too big. It fell down and covered Anna's whole body.

Lily tried to pull the lamp shade off, but it was stuck. She pulled harder and harder. She did not see the cord of the lamp. She pulled the cord and the lamp fell off the desk. It hit the floor and broke. Glass and wires flew everywhere.

Lily was scared. She heard her mom scream. She ran to her mom and hugged her. Her mom was angry and sad. She saw the broken lamp and Anna under the lamp shade. She saw blood on Lily's hand. Lily had cut herself on the glass.

Her mom took Lily to the bathroom and cleaned her wound. She put a bandage on it. She told Lily she was very naughty and careless. She said Lily had to pay for the lamp and Anna. She said Lily could not play with her toys for a week.

Lily cried and cried. She was sorry and hurt. She wanted her lamp and Anna back. She wanted her mom to love her. She did not like the bad ending.

Lila and Sam were excited to see the fireworks. They put on their coats and hats and followed Mom and Dad to the park. There were many people and cars and lights.

"Can we sit close to the fireworks, Mom?" Lila asked.

"No, sweetie, we have to sit far away. The fireworks are very loud and bright. They can hurt your ears and eyes if you are too close," Mom said.

"But I want to see them better," Sam said.

"Don't worry, you will see them very well from here. Look, they are starting!" Dad said.

Lila and Sam looked up and saw the fireworks. They were red and blue and green and yellow. They made shapes like stars and flowers and hearts. They also made loud noises like bangs and pops and whistles.

Lila and Sam clapped and cheered. They liked the fireworks. They were pretty and fun.

But there was a man who did not like the fireworks. He was sitting next to them. He was deaf. He could not hear the fireworks. He could only see them. He did not think they were pretty or fun. He thought they were scary and annoying.

He covered his eyes with his hands. He shook his head. He said, "Stop, stop, stop!"

Lila and Sam saw the man. They felt sorry for him. They wanted to help him.

They went to him and said, "Hello, sir. We are Lila and Sam. We like the fireworks. Do you not like them?"

The man looked at them. He saw their mouths moving. He did not hear their words. He did not understand them.

He said, "I am deaf. I cannot hear you. I cannot hear the fireworks. I only see them. They hurt my eyes. They make me sad."

Lila and Sam nodded. They understood. They said, "We are sorry. We did not know. We want you to be happy. Do you want to work with us?"

The man was curious. He said, "Work? What work?"

Lila and Sam smiled. They said, "We have a work. We have a book. It has pictures of animals and colors and numbers. We can show you the book. We can learn the book. We can have fun with the book."

The man thought for a moment. He said, "Okay. I will work with you. I will see the book. Maybe I will like the book."

Lila and Sam were happy. They took the man's hand and led him to their blanket. They gave him the book. They opened the book. They pointed to the pictures. They said the names. They made signs with their hands.

The man watched them. He learned the names. He learned the signs. He smiled. He liked the book. He liked Lila and Sam.

They worked and played with the book. They forgot about the fireworks. They had fun. They made a new friend.

Jill and Tom were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they found a golf ball in their yard. They wondered who left it there.

"Maybe it's from the big house next door," Jill said. "They have a lot of golf things."

"Let's go see," Tom said. "Maybe they will let us play with them."

They walked to the big house and knocked on the door. No one answered. They heard a mysterious noise from the back yard. It sounded like a swing and a hit.

"Come on, let's check it out," Tom said. He was curious and brave.

"I don't know, Tom," Jill said. She was careful and scared. "Maybe we should go back home."

But Tom did not listen. He ran to the back yard and saw a man with a golf club and a bag of golf balls. He was practicing his shots.

"Hi, mister," Tom said. "Can we play with you?"

The man turned around and saw Tom. He was angry and mean.

"Who are you? How did you get here? Go away, this is my golf course!" he shouted.

He swung his golf club at Tom and hit him on the head. Tom fell down and cried.

Jill heard Tom's cry and ran to help him. She saw the man and the golf club and the blood. She was shocked and sad.

"Tom, Tom, are you okay?" she asked. She hugged him and tried to stop the bleeding.

The man saw Jill and felt sorry and ashamed. He realized he had hurt a child.

"I'm sorry, I'm sorry, I didn't mean to do that," he said. He put down his golf club and called for help.

Jill and Tom were taken to the hospital. They had to stay there for a few days. The man came to visit them and apologized again. He brought them some toys and books and candy. He said he was lonely and angry and did not like people. He said he learned his lesson and wanted to be a better person.

Jill and Tom forgave him and became his friends. They taught him how to share and be kind and have fun. They played golf with him sometimes, but only with soft balls and gentle swings.

The moral of the story is: don't be rude and violent to strangers, they might be children who want to play with you. And don't go to places where you are not invited, they might be dangerous and scary. And always listen to your sister, she might be smarter and wiser than you.

Lily smiled and said, "I love you too, Ben." She gave him a kiss and a hug. Then she whistled a little song, but very softly. She fell asleep in her crib, happy and peaceful.

The moral of the story is: Whistling is fun, but you have to respect others and be quiet when they need to sleep. You also have to be kind and forgive when someone is bitter and says mean things.

"I don't know. Maybe it has a home. Maybe it is lost," Ben says.

They go near the dog. The dog wags its tail and licks their hands. They pet the dog and give it some water. The dog is happy.

"Can we keep the dog?" Sara asks Ben.

"I don't know. Maybe someone is looking for it. Maybe it has a name," Ben says.

They look at the dog's collar. It has a tag with a phone number and a name. The name is Max.

"Let's call the number. Maybe we can find Max's home," Ben says.

They use Sara's mom's phone to call the number. A woman answers. She sounds worried.

"Hello? Is this Max's owner?" Ben asks.

"Yes, yes, this is Max's owner. Do you have Max? Where is he? I've been looking for him all day. He ran away from the yard. The lock on the gate was broken," the woman says.

"We have Max. He is in the park. He is cute and friendly. We gave him some water. He likes us," Ben says.

"OK, we will stay with him. We hope you come soon. We like Max, but we know he is your dog," Ben says.

Sara and Ben are happy. They say goodbye to Max. They learned a lesson. They learned to help others and to respect their belongings. They hope to see Max again. They are still friends. They go home.

"I'm trying, Tom, but the boat is too heavy!" Sam says.

They row and row, but the boat is slow. The storm is closer and closer. Suddenly, a big wave hits the boat. The boat breaks. The wood cracks and the cloth tears. The boat sinks. Tom and Sam fall into the water.

"Help, help!" they shout.

They swim and swim, but the shore is far. The water is cold and deep. They are tired and scared. They think they will drown.

But then, they see a light. It is their dad. He has a small boat with a motor. He heard their shouts. He came to save them.

"Tom, Sam, hold on, I'm coming!" he says.

He drives the boat to them. He pulls them out of the water. He wraps them in a blanket. He takes them to the shore.

"Are you okay, boys?" he asks.

"Yes, dad, we are okay, thank you!" they say.

They hug their dad. They are happy and relieved. They are safe.

But they are also sad. They look at their big boat. It is broken and sunk. They worked hard to make it. They had fun with it. They love it.

"Dad, can we fix our boat?" they ask.

"Maybe, boys, maybe. But it will take a lot of work and time. And you have to be careful next time. The lake can be dangerous. You have to watch the weather and stay close to the shore. Do you understand?" he says.

"Yes, dad, we understand. We are sorry. We will be careful. And we will fix our boat. Together." they say.

They smile. They have learned a lesson. They have their dad. They have each other. They have hope.

Lily and Ben were twins. They liked to play outside in the fall. They saw many leaves on the ground. They were red, yellow and brown. They picked up some leaves and threw them in the air.

"Look, Lily, look!" Ben said. "The leaves are flying like birds!"

Lily laughed and clapped her hands. She saw something big and orange in the corner of the yard. She ran to it and touched it. It was hard and cold.

"Ben, Ben, come here!" Lily called. "I found a pumpkin!"

Ben ran to Lily and saw the pumpkin too. It was bigger than their heads. It had a green stem and some dirt on it.
