"I don't know, Ben," Lily said. "Maybe it grew from a seed. Maybe someone left it here for us."

Lily and Ben hugged the pumpkin. They wanted to make it their friend. They decided to give it a name.

"Let's call it Jack," Lily said.

"OK, let's call it Jack," Ben agreed.

They smiled and looked at Jack. They thought he looked happy too. They wanted to take him inside and show him to their mom and dad. They tried to lift him, but he was too heavy.

"Jack, you are too heavy!" Lily said.

"Jack, you need to eat less!" Ben said.

They laughed and looked for a wagon. They found one in the garage. They put Jack on the wagon and pulled him to the door. They knocked and waited for their mom and dad to open.

"Mom, Dad, look!" Lily and Ben said. "We found a pumpkin! His name is Jack!"

Mom and Dad opened the door and saw Jack. They were surprised and happy.

"Wow, Lily and Ben, what a big pumpkin!" Mom said.

"Where did you find him?" Dad asked.

"We found him in the yard," Lily said.

"He's our friend," Ben said.

Mom and Dad smiled and hugged Lily and Ben. They helped them bring Jack inside. They put him on the table and gave him a face. They carved two eyes, a nose and a mouth. They put a candle inside and turned off the lights. Jack glowed and looked spooky.

"Look, Lily, look!" Ben said. "Jack is glowing!"

Lily laughed and clapped her hands. She saw Jack's face and liked it.

"Jack, you are glowing!" Lily said.

"Jack, you are spooky!" Ben said.

They hugged Jack and thanked him for being their friend. They told him stories and sang songs. They had a lot of fun with Jack. They were happy and warm. They forgot about the cold outside.

One day, Sara and her mom went to the zoo and saw a sign that said "Rhinoceros Feeding Time". Sara was very excited and wanted to see the rhinoceros eat. She asked her mom if they could go closer to the fence. Her mom said yes, but told her to be careful and not touch the fence.

She wanted to say hello to the rhinoceros and make friends with it. She leaned over the fence and waved her hand. She said "Hi, rhinoceros! You are very nice. Can I pet you?"

The rhinoceros heard Sara's voice and looked up. It saw Sara's hand and thought it was food. It opened its mouth and moved its head towards Sara. Sara did not know what the rhinoceros wanted. She thought it wanted to play with her. She smiled and moved her hand closer.

Her mom saw what was happening and got very worried. She knew the rhinoceros could hurt Sara with its teeth or horn. She shouted "Sara, no! Don't touch the rhinoceros! It might bite you!" She grabbed Sara's arm and pulled her back from the fence.

Sara calmed down and said "I love you too, mom. I'm sorry I made you worried. I didn't know the rhinoceros was wild. Can we still watch it eat?"

Her mom said "Yes, we can. But we have to stay away from the fence and not touch it. OK?"

The people and animals worked together to rebuild their town, and soon the town was back to normal. From then on, they always remained prepared and ready in case another flood ever happened.

"Look, Ben, I found a blue bug!" Lily said, holding up a shiny beetle. "It is so pretty!"

"Wow, Lily, that is a nice bug!" Ben said. "Can I see it?"

Lily gave Ben the jar. He looked at the blue bug. It had big eyes and long legs. He wanted to touch it.

"Be careful, Ben," Lily said. "Mommy said some bugs can bite or sting. Maybe this bug is spicy."

Ben did not listen. He opened the jar and reached for the blue bug. He wanted to feel it. But the blue bug did not like that. It made a loud noise and flew out of the jar. It buzzed around Ben's head and landed on his nose.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Ben cried. "The blue bug is spicy! It bit me!"

Lily heard Ben cry. She ran to him and saw the blue bug on his nose. She was scared. She grabbed a leaf and tried to shoo the blue bug away. But the blue bug did not want to leave. It made more noise and flew around Lily's head.

"Help, help, help!" Lily shouted. "The blue bug is angry! It wants to bite me too!"

Mommy heard Lily and Ben shout. She came to the garden and saw the blue bug. She knew what it was. It was a wasp. A wasp is a bad bug that can hurt people. She took a newspaper and swatted the wasp. She made it go away.

"Are you okay, Ben and Lily?" Mommy asked. "What happened?"

"We found a blue bug, Mommy," Lily said. "But it was not a nice bug. It was a spicy bug. It bit Ben and tried to bite me."

Mommy hugged Ben and Lily. She looked at Ben's nose. It was red and swollen. She put some ice on it and gave him a kiss.

"I'm sorry, Ben," Mommy said. "That was not a blue bug. That was a wasp. A wasp is a bad bug that can hurt people. You should not touch it or open the jar. You should leave it alone."

"I'm sorry, Mommy," Ben said. "I did not know. It looked pretty. But it was spicy. It hurt me."

Mommy smiled. She gave Lily a kiss too.

"You were brave, Lily," Mommy said. "You tried to help Ben. But next time, if you see a wasp, you should run away and call me. I will help you."

"Okay, Mommy," Lily said. "We will not play with wasps anymore. We will only play with nice bugs."

But then, they heard their mom coming back. They got scared and tried to hide the jar and the spoons. They ran to the living room and hid behind the couch. But they were too messy. They had jelly on their faces, their hands, and their clothes. Their mom saw them and knew what they did.

She was very upset. She said, "Tom and Sam, you were very naughty. You took the jelly without asking. You lied and you made a mess. You have to say sorry and help me clean up. And no more jelly for you today."

Tom and Sam felt bad. They said sorry and helped their mom. They learned their lesson. They knew that stealing and lying were wrong. They decided to be good and ask for jelly next time. They hoped their mom would forgive them and give them some jelly tomorrow.

Lily was a good girl who liked to help her mom and dad. She was obedient and did what they told her. One day, her mom asked her to go to the store and buy some milk and eggs. She gave her some money and a list.

Lily put on her coat and shoes and walked to the store. She saw many people and cars on the way. She said hello to some of them. She also saw a network of wires on the poles. She wondered what they were for.

When she got to the store, she looked for the milk and eggs. She found them in the fridge. She took one carton of each and went to the cashier. The cashier was a nice lady who smiled at her. She scanned the items and told Lily how much they cost.

Lily gave her the money and waited for the change. The cashier gave her some coins and a receipt. She also gave her a sticker with a star on it. She said, "You are a very smart and obedient girl. I recommend that you keep up the good work. Here is a sticker for you."

Lily thanked her and put the sticker on her coat. She felt happy and proud. She put the milk and eggs in a bag and walked back home. She gave them to her mom and showed her the sticker. Her mom hugged her and said, "You are a wonderful daughter. I love you very much." Lily smiled and said, "I love you too, mom."

Ben and Lily were playing in the sand. They liked to dig and make castles and tunnels. Ben had a spade, a big tool for digging. Lily had a bucket, a round thing for holding sand.

"Look, Lily, I found something shiny!" Ben said. He used his spade to dig out a shiny thing from the sand. It was a ring, a small circle of metal that people wear on their fingers.

"Wow, Ben, that's pretty! Can I see?" Lily asked. She reached out her hand to take the ring.

"No, it's mine! I found it!" Ben said. He pulled the ring away from Lily. He was greedy, he wanted to keep the ring for himself.

"Please, Ben, let me see. Just for a moment. I won't take it, I promise," Lily said. She was sad, she wanted to see the ring too.

"Fine, but only for a moment. And don't touch it!" Ben said. He held the ring close to Lily's face, but not too close. He was afraid she would grab it.

Lily looked at the ring. She saw something on it, some small words. She was clever, she knew how to read some words. She read the words on the ring.

"Ben, this ring is not good. It says 'Danger. Do not touch. Explodes when exposed to air.' You have to put it back in the sand, now!" Lily said. She was scared, she knew the ring could hurt them.

"What? No, you're lying. You just want the ring for yourself. You're not clever, you're silly. This ring is mine, and it's beautiful. I'm not putting it back!" Ben said. He was angry, he didn't believe Lily. He thought she was trying to trick him.

"Ben, please, listen to me. It's not a lie, it's the truth. The ring is bad, it can explode. Please, put it back, before it's too late!" Lily said. She was crying, she wanted to save Ben and herself.

But Ben didn't listen. He didn't put the ring back. He kept holding it in his hand. He smiled, he thought he was lucky.

Then, the ring exploded. It made a loud noise, and a bright flash. It hurt Ben and Lily very much. They fell to the ground, and didn't get up. The ring was gone, and so were they. It was a bad ending.

Ben and Lily were twins who liked to play together. They had many toys, but their favorite was a big red car that they could ride in the yard. One day, their mom told them it was time for a nap. She said they had to be obedient and go to their beds, or they would not get any mail.

"What is mail?" Ben asked.

"Mail is something that comes in a box or an envelope. Sometimes it has a surprise inside, like a sticker or a card. Mommy and Daddy get mail from their friends and family. And sometimes, you get mail too, if you are good and nap," mom explained.

Ben and Lily wanted to get mail, so they nodded and went to their beds. They tried to sleep, but they were not very tired. They heard mom go to the kitchen and turn on the radio. They whispered to each other.

"Let's sneak out and play with the car," Ben said.

"Okay, but we have to be quiet," Lily agreed.

They got out of their beds and tiptoed to the door. They opened it slowly and looked around. They saw mom in the kitchen, busy with something. They did not see dad, who was working in his office. They ran to the yard and got in the car. They laughed and drove around, pretending to be race drivers.

They did not hear the mailman come to the door. He rang the bell and left a big box on the porch. He also left a small envelope with Ben and Lily's names on it. He did not see the twins in the car, because they were behind a bush.

Mom heard the bell and went to the door. She saw the box and the envelope. She smiled and picked them up. She went to the kitchen and opened the box. It was a cake from grandma, who lived far away. She opened the envelope. It was a card from grandma, with a picture of a cat and a dog. Inside, there were two stickers, one for Ben and one for Lily.

Mom was happy and wanted to share the cake and the stickers with the twins. She went to their room and opened the door. She saw their empty beds and their toys on the floor. She was angry and worried. She called their names, but they did not answer. She looked out the window and saw the car in the yard. She ran outside and saw Ben and Lily in the car. They saw her and stopped. They looked scared.

"Ben and Lily, what are you doing? You were supposed to nap! You were not obedient! You missed the mail!" mom yelled.

Ben and Lily got out of the car and hung their heads. They felt sorry and ashamed. They did not know about the cake and the stickers. They only wanted to have fun.

Mom took them by the hand and brought them inside. She put the cake and the stickers on the table. She said they could not have any, because they were bad. She said they had to go back to their beds and stay there until dinner. She said they had to think about what they did and say sorry.

Ben and Lily cried and said sorry. They went to their beds and lay down. They did not play or talk. They wished they had napped and got the mail. They wished they had been obedient. They learned their lesson. The end.

They were having fun, but they did not notice that they also made some marks on the wall. The wall was white and now it had red and blue lines on it.

Mom came into the living room and saw the wall. She was not happy. She said to Lily and Ben, "Who did this? You know you are not supposed to draw on the wall. That is naughty."

Lily and Ben felt sorry. They did not mean to make Mom angry. They said, "We are sorry, Mom. We did not see the wall. We only wanted to draw pictures."

Lily and Ben nodded. They took the sponge and the water and went to the wall. They tried to remove the crayon marks, but it was hard. The crayons were sticky and did not come off easily.

Lily had an idea. She was clever. She said to Ben, "I know what we can do. We can draw more pictures on the wall, but with white crayons. Then the wall will look white again."

Ben thought that was a good idea. He was clever too. He said, "Yes, let's do that. Mom will not see the crayon marks anymore."

They found some white crayons and started to draw over the red and blue lines. They made white fish, white rockets, white flowers and white cars. They were happy. They thought they fixed the wall.

Mom came back to the living room and saw the wall. She was surprised. She said, "What did you do? You did not remove the crayon marks. You made more of them. But they are white. How did you do that?"

Lily and Ben smiled. They said, "We used white crayons, Mom. We are clever. We made the wall white again."

Mom did not know what to say. She was amazed. She said, "You are clever, indeed. But you are also silly. You still have to remove the crayon marks. White crayons are still crayons. They do not belong on the wall. Come on, let's try again. And next time, please draw only on paper."

Ben and Lily were playing with their toys in the garden. They had a lot of fun with their cars, dolls, and blocks. But Ben's favorite toy was a blue snowman that his owner, Mom, had made for him last winter. He kept it in the freezer and took it out only on very hot days.

"Look, Lily, this is my blue snowman!" Ben said, showing his toy to his sister. "He is very cold and hard, but he is also very nice and friendly. Do you want to touch him?"

Lily nodded and reached out her hand. She felt the snowman's nose, eyes, and mouth. They were made of carrots, buttons, and a scarf. She smiled and said, "He is very cute, Ben. But why is he blue?"

"Mom said he is blue because he is special. He is not like the other snowmen. He can stay with me all year long, even when there is no snow. He is my best friend," Ben said, hugging his snowman.

But then, something bad happened. The sun was very bright and hot that day, and it shone on the snowman. The snowman started to feel warm and wet. He began to melt.

"Ben, look, your snowman is melting!" Lily cried, pointing at the toy. "He is getting smaller and smaller. He is losing his nose, his eyes, and his mouth. He is not blue anymore. He is white and clear. What can we do?"

Ben felt very sad and scared. He did not want to lose his blue snowman. He did not want him to melt away. He ran to the freezer and opened the door. He tried to put his snowman inside, but it was too late. His snowman was gone. He only had a puddle of water in his hands.

"Mom, Mom, help me!" Ben shouted, tears running down his face. "My blue snowman melted. He is gone. I miss him. I want him back."

Mom heard Ben's cry and came to the garden. She saw Ben and Lily and the water on the floor. She felt sorry for Ben and hugged him.

"I'm sorry, Ben. I know you loved your blue snowman. But you know, snowmen are not meant to last forever. They are made of snow, and snow melts when it gets warm. That's how nature works. But that doesn't mean your blue snowman is gone forever. He is still here, in a different form. He is water now, and water is very important for life. Water can make plants grow, animals drink, and rainbows appear. Water can also freeze again, and become snow. Maybe, next winter, you can make another blue snowman, or a different color, or a different shape. You can use your imagination and have fun. And you can always remember your blue snowman in your heart. He will always be your friend, no matter what," Mom said, wiping Ben's tears.

Ben listened to Mom and felt a little better. He looked at the water and smiled. He said, "Thank you, Mom. You are right. Water is very nice and useful. And maybe I can make another snowman someday. But I will never forget my blue snowman. He was very special to me. I love him."

Lily hugged Ben and said, "I love him too, Ben. He was very cute and friendly. And I love you, Ben. You are my brother. And I love Mom. She is our owner. And I love our toys. They are our friends. We have a lot of things to love, Ben. And a lot of things to play with. Come on, let's play some more. Maybe we can make a water slide with the hose. That would be fun."

Ben nodded and smiled. He said, "Okay, Lily. Let's play some more. That would be fun. And maybe we can see a rainbow too. That would be beautiful."

Mom smiled and said, "That's a good idea, kids. Have fun. And don't forget to drink some water too. It's good for you."

"Maybe he does not talk," Lily said. "Maybe he is shy."

Ben and Lily decided to give the owl a name. They thought of different names, but they did not like any of them. They wanted to give the owl an original name. A name that no other owl had.

"Forget?" Lily asked. "Why Forget?"

"Because he forgets to talk!" Ben said. "And because we will never forget him!"

Lily liked the name. She thought it was funny and cute. She nodded.

But they did not know that the teacher was looking for them. She was worried and angry. She asked the other children where Anna and Ben were. She found out that they had left the classroom. She went to the playground to find them.

Anna and Ben saw the teacher coming. They were frightened. They knew they had done something bad. They tried to hide behind a tree. But the teacher saw them. She called their names. She told them to come to her.

Anna and Ben came out of their hiding place. They looked at the teacher. They felt sorry. They said, "We are sorry, teacher. We wanted to play. We did not want to nap."

The teacher said, "I understand, Anna and Ben. But you have to follow the rules. Napping is good for you. It helps you grow and learn. And you have to stay with the class. It is not safe to go to the playground alone. You could get hurt or lost. Do you understand?"

Anna and Ben nodded. They said, "Yes, teacher. We understand. We will not do it again."

The teacher said, "I am glad you understand. Now, let's go back to the classroom. You have to finish your nap. And then you can play again with your friends."

Anna and Ben followed the teacher. They held hands. They learned their lesson. They still liked to play. But they also liked to nap.

Tom and Sam are friends. They like to play with cars and balls in the park. One day, they find a big stick on the ground. Tom picks up the stick and says, "This is my sword. I am a knight."

Sam wants the stick too. He says, "No, this is my sword. I am a king." They both pull the stick and try to take it from each other. They are angry and loud.

A bird is sitting on a tree nearby. The bird likes the park. It is peaceful and green. The bird does not like the noise and the fighting. The bird flies down and strikes the stick with its beak. The stick breaks in two. Tom and Sam are surprised and scared. They drop the stick and run away.

The bird is happy. It has stopped the fight. It sings a song and flies back to the tree. The park is peaceful again.

Lily and Ben were at the beach with their mom and dad. They liked to play in the sand and splash in the water. They saw many things in the sea, like fish, crabs, and shells. But they also saw something that scared them: jellyfish.

"Look, mom, jellyfish!" Lily pointed at the water. "They are big and shiny and have long arms. Can we touch them?"

"No, sweetie, you can't touch them. They can hurt you. They have stingers that can make you feel very bad. Stay away from them, okay?" Mom said.

Lily and Ben nodded. They did not want to feel bad. They wanted to have fun. They decided to climb on the rocks instead. The rocks were high and rough and had holes and cracks. They liked to pretend they were explorers, looking for treasure.

They climbed and climbed, until they reached the top of the biggest rock. They felt very proud and happy. They could see the whole beach and the sea. They saw their mom and dad waving at them. They waved back.

"Wow, this is amazing!" Ben said. "We are so high!"

"Yes, we are!" Lily said. "But be careful, Ben. Don't go too close to the edge. You might fall."

Ben did not listen. He wanted to see more. He walked to the edge of the rock and leaned over. He saw something shiny in the water. He thought it was a treasure. He reached out his hand to grab it.

But it was not a treasure. It was a jellyfish. And it stung him.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Ben cried. "It hurts, it hurts, it hurts!"

Lily heard him and ran to him. She saw his hand was red and swollen. She was very scared. She shouted for help.

"Mom, dad, help! Ben touched a jellyfish! He is hurt!"

Mom and dad heard her and ran to them. They saw Ben's hand and felt very sorry for him. They took him down from the rock and wrapped his hand in a towel. They took him to the doctor, who gave him some medicine and a bandage.

The doctor told Ben he would be okay, but he had to be more careful next time. He told him not to touch jellyfish or anything else that looked dangerous. He told him to listen to his mom and dad and his sister.

Ben nodded. He felt very sorry and sad. He said sorry to Lily, who hugged him and said it was okay. She said she loved him and he was her best friend.

They went back to the beach and played in the sand and splash in the water. They did not climb on the rocks or touch the jellyfish. They had fun and were safe. They learned a lesson and were happy.

One day, Sara's cousin Ben came to visit. Ben was older and liked to tease Sara. He saw Lily and said, "What a silly doll! She is old and dirty. You should throw her away and get a new one." Ben laughed and said, "Magic? There is no such thing as magic. Watch this!" He grabbed Lily and ran outside. He threw her in the mud and stomped on her. Sara cried and ran after him. She tried to get Lily back, but Ben was too fast and strong.

Sara saw a big stick on the ground. She picked it up and swung it at Ben. She hit him on the leg and he fell down. He dropped Lily and said, "Ow! That hurt! You are a bad girl!" Sara ignored him and ran to Lily. She hugged her and said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I love you. You are still magic to me."

Sara's mom came out and saw what happened. She scolded Ben and told him to apologize. She praised Sara and said, "You are very brave, Sara. You stood up for yourself and your friend. You showed Ben that magic is not something you can see, but something you can feel. You should always cherish your magic and never let anyone spoil it." Sara smiled and thanked her mom. She cleaned Lily and gave her a kiss. She felt happy and proud. She knew Lily was magic, and so was she.

Leo said, "Let's play tag. You're it!" He tapped her shoulder and ran away. Mia chased him around the park. They ran past the swings, the sandbox, and the fountain. They had a lot of fun.

She thought, "Children are so good at making friends. They don't care about the color of their hair or their eyes. They just care about having fun." She called Mia and said, "It's time to go home, sweetie. Say goodbye to Leo."

Mia said, "Okay. See you tomorrow." She waved at him and ran to her mom. She held her mom's hand and said, "Mom, I had a lot of fun today. I met a new friend. His name is Leo. He has black hair and black eyes. He's very nice."

Mia smiled and said, "Thank you, mom. I love you."

Her mom said, "I love you too, Mia." They walked home together, happy and warm.

They take their bucket and shovel and start to clean the shore. They find some of their shells and some new ones. They make new castles and decorate them with shells. They lean on their castles and smile. They are happy again.

"Look, Ben, look!" Jill shouted. "I found a shiny thing. It is very pretty and sparkly. What is it?"

"Maybe it is a diamond," he said. "Diamonds are very rare and very valuable. They are in stories and movies. Maybe we are rich now!"

Jill was curious. She wanted to know more about the diamond. She wondered how it felt and how it tasted. She asked Ben if she could have it back.

"Can I have the diamond, please?" she said. "I want to touch it and taste it. Maybe it is sweet or sour or salty."

Ben was surprised. He did not think that tasting the diamond was a good idea. He thought that it might be hard or sharp or dirty. He did not want Jill to hurt herself or get sick.

"No, Jill, no!" he said. "You cannot taste the diamond. It is not food. It is not for eating. It is for keeping or selling or giving. Tasting the diamond is silly and dangerous. Give it to me."

Jill was sad and angry. She did not like Ben's words. She did not think that he was being nice or fair. She wanted to try the diamond for herself. She thought that it might be fun or yummy or special. She did not want to give it to him.

"No, Ben, no!" she said. "You cannot have the diamond. It is mine. I found it first. I want to taste it. Tasting the diamond is fun and brave and clever. Give it to me."

Then, something bad happened. The diamond broke. It split into two pieces. It was not shiny or sparkly anymore. It was dull and cracked and sad. Jill and Ben were shocked and sorry. They had ruined the diamond. They had ruined their game. They had ruined their day.

Once upon a time, there lived a black cat. The cat was very ignorant and did not know much about the world. All day, he would sleep in the sun and not do anything else.

One day, the sun started to shine brighter than usual. The cat decided to go for a walk and explore the world a little bit. As the sun was too strong for the cat, it started to feel very hot. Everyone else in the village was hiding in the shade, but the cat kept walking.

After a while of exploring, the cat noticed something bright ahead of him. He realized it was a shiny diamond lying on the ground. The black cat was very excited and used his paw to pick it up. It felt so cold and smooth in its paws.

The cat was very happy and proud of his find. He then brought the diamond back home and kept it safe. From then on, whenever the sun was shining, the cat would bring out his diamond and put it in the sun. It would always sparkle and shine so brightly that everyone would be so amazed.

A farmer was walking through the field with a wagon full of hay. The little lamb watched him intently, and when the farmer started to walk away, the little lamb decided to follow him.

The lamb followed the farmer, who was humming to himself. The little lamb hopped and skipped along, never leaving the farmer's side. As they continued, the farmer looked down and saw the little lamb following him. He smiled and gave her a pat, inviting her to join him.

The farmer and the little lamb continued walking, side by side. Eventually they made it to the barn, the wagon full of hay still in tow. The farmer showed the little lamb the hay, and showed her how to sleep on it. From that day, the lamb always wanted to go back to the barn with the farmer and sleep in the hay.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Molly. She was 3 years old and loved playing in the garden.

One day, she saw something in the corner of her garden that she hadn't seen before - a blackboard.

"What's that?" she said in excitement.

Molly picked up a piece of chalk and started to draw on the blackboard. But when she tried to draw a circle, it didn't look right so she became frustrated.

Then she heard a quiet whisper coming from beside the blackboard. It said: "Remember to draw small circles - that's how you get the right shape".

Molly looked around but couldn't see anyone. She looked back at the blackboard and tried drawing again - this time making much smaller circles. She felt very pleased with herself when the circle she drew looked perfect!

Molly gave a huge smile, thanked the mysterious whisperer and went back inside for her supper.

The panda was so scared, he wanted to run away. But suddenly, he heard a small voice. "I'm stuck inside the cave, please help me!"
 
The panda felt brave and started to dig in the hole, freeing the creature inside. It was a small mouse! The mouse shouted with happiness and the panda felt so proud.

They thanked each other and the panda said goodbye. He was so dizzy from all of the digging, but so happy that he could help the little mouse. He went back to his home in the forest, feeling much better than before.

Tweety thought hard and finally came up with a plan. He flew back to the tree branch and carefully untangled the thread from the branches. "Dad, we are sorry. We were playing castle. We did not know the sofa and the cushions were modern. And we did not know the necklace was mom's. We will put everything back and say sorry to mom," Lisa said, in a small voice.

Dad sighed and calmed down. He remembered how he used to play when he was a kid. He knew they were just using their imagination.

"Okay, kids, I forgive you. But you have to be more careful and respectful of other people's things. And you have to clean up after yourselves. Now, go and put everything back where it belongs, and then come and give me a hug," he said.

Lisa and Tom nodded and did as they were told. They put the cushions and blankets back on the sofa, and the necklace back in the drawer. Then they ran to their dad and hugged him. They said they loved him and they were sorry.

Dad hugged them back and said he loved them too. He was not angry anymore. He was proud of his kids and their creativity. He decided to play castle with them tomorrow, and maybe even wear a crown.

One day, a little turtle wanted to see the big sea. He was tired of living in the pond with his family. He said to his mother, "I want to go to the sea. It is big and blue and fun."

His mother said, "No, you are too small to go to the sea. It is far and dangerous and scary. You will get lost or hurt or eaten by big fish. You must stay in the pond. It is safe and warm and good."

But the little turtle did not listen. He waited until his mother was asleep, and then he crawled out of the pond. He crawled and crawled and crawled, until he saw the sea. It was big and blue and fun, just like he imagined. He was happy and excited. He crawled to the shore and dipped his feet in the water.

But he did not know that the sea was not easy. It was strong and wild and loud. It pushed and pulled and splashed him. He was scared and cold and wet. He wanted to go back to the pond. He wanted to see his mother. He cried and cried and cried.

Then he saw a big shadow in the water. It was a big fish. It had sharp teeth and hungry eyes. It saw the little turtle and wanted to eat him. It swam fast and opened its mouth. The little turtle was very afraid. He had no place to hide. He thought he was going to die.

But then he heard a voice. It was his mother. She had followed him to the sea. She saw the big fish and the little turtle. She was brave and smart. She bit the big fish's tail and made it go away. She saved the little turtle. She hugged him and said, "I love you, my son. You are safe now. Let's go back to the pond. It is our home."

The little turtle was sorry and thankful. He said, "I love you, too, mother. You are right. The sea is not for me. The pond is my home. I will never leave you again."

They crawled back to the pond. They were happy and warm and good. The little turtle learned his lesson. He never tried to go to the sea again. He stayed in the pond with his family. He was wise and happy and good.

Lily liked to grow flowers in her garden. She had a small pot with soil and seeds. Every day, she watered the soil and waited for the seeds to grow. She hoped they would grow into pretty flowers.

One day, she heard a loud noise outside. She ran to the window and saw a big truck. The truck was digging up the road near her house. It made a lot of dust and noise. Lily was scared. She covered her ears and hid under her bed.

She forgot about her pot with soil and seeds. She did not water it for many days. The soil became dry and hard. The seeds did not grow. They stayed small and brown.

Lily's mom saw the pot and felt sad. She knew Lily loved flowers. She took the pot and put it in the kitchen. She watered the soil and put it near the window. She hoped the seeds would grow.

After a few days, the truck left. The road was fixed. It was quiet again. Lily came out of her bed. She saw her pot in the kitchen. She saw something green poking out of the soil. She saw tiny buds on the green stems. She smiled. Her seeds were growing. They were growing into flowers.

Lily and Ben were twins who loved to visit their grandma on the farm. They liked to feed the chickens, pet the cows and watch the pigs roll in the mud. But their favorite animals were the sheep. The sheep were soft, white and playful. They liked to run, jump and bleat.

One day, Lily and Ben decided to play hide and seek with the sheep. They took turns hiding behind the trees, the barn and the fence, while the other one counted and looked for them. The sheep joined in the fun, following them around and hiding with them.

Lily was hiding behind a big rock, while Ben was counting to ten. She heard a loud noise and peeked out. She saw a big, black dog running towards the sheep. The dog was barking and growling. The sheep were scared and started to tremble. They ran away from the dog, but the dog was faster and chased them.

Lily was afraid too. She wanted to help the sheep, but she did not know what to do. She shouted for Ben.

"Ben, Ben, come quick! There is a bad dog chasing the sheep!"

Ben heard Lily's voice and stopped counting. He ran to where she was hiding and saw the dog and the sheep. He was brave and picked up a stick. He waved the stick at the dog and yelled.

"Go away, dog! Leave the sheep alone! They are our friends!"

The dog saw Ben and the stick and stopped. He was not so brave anymore. He turned around and ran away, back to where he came from.

Lily and Ben hugged each other. They were happy and relieved. They ran to the sheep and checked if they were okay. The sheep were okay, but still trembling. Lily and Ben petted them and talked to them softly.

"It's okay, sheep. The dog is gone. You are safe now. We are sorry that he scared you."

The sheep calmed down and thanked Lily and Ben with their bleats. They nuzzled them and licked them. They were grateful and happy. They were playful again.

Lily and Ben smiled and laughed. They played with the sheep some more, until their grandma called them for lunch. They said goodbye to the sheep and promised to come back soon. They loved the sheep and the sheep loved them. They were friends.

"No, Ben, this bread is for the ducks. You have your own bread in your bag. You can eat it later," Anna says. She thinks Ben is not fair. She wants to share the bread with the ducks, not with Ben.

"But I want some bread now. Please, Anna, give me some bread," Ben says. He tries to grab the bread from Anna's hand. Anna pulls the bread away. She is angry.

"Stop it, Ben! You are not nice. You are not my friend. Go away!" Anna says. She runs away from Ben. She stays near the pond. She feeds the ducks more bread.

One day, a boy named Sam went to the park with his mom. He saw a big slide and wanted to go on it. He ran to the slide and climbed up the steps. He was very happy.

But when he reached the top, he saw a big bear sitting on the slide. The bear was brown and furry and had a red scarf around his neck. He looked at Sam and said, "Hello, little boy. Do you want to slide with me?"

Sam was scared of the bear. He did not want to slide with him. He wanted to go back to his mom. He said, "No, thank you, Mr. Bear. I have to go now. Please move away from the slide."

But the bear did not move. He ignored Sam and said, "Oh, come on, little boy. Don't be afraid. I am a friendly bear. I just want to have some fun. Let's slide together. It will be fun."

Sam did not like the bear. He did not think he was friendly. He thought he was mean and rude. He said, "No, Mr. Bear. I don't want to slide with you. You are blocking the slide. You are not nice. Please go away."

But the bear still ignored Sam and said, "Fine, little boy. If you don't want to slide with me, I will slide by myself. Watch me go. Whee!" And he pushed himself down the slide.

Sam was angry and sad. He did not get to slide. He saw the bear slide down and land on the ground. He saw the bear get up and run away. He saw the slide open and empty. He wanted to slide, but he did not want to slide after the bear. He thought the slide was dirty and smelly now. He did not want to touch it.

He ran back to his mom and told her what happened. His mom hugged him and said, "I'm sorry, Sam. That was a bad bear. He should not have blocked the slide. He should not have ignored you. He should have been polite and shared. You did the right thing to say no to him. You are a good boy."

Sam felt better. He said, "Thank you, mom. I love you. Can we go to the swings instead?"

His mom smiled and said, "Of course, Sam. I love you too. Let's go to the swings. They are open and fun." And they walked to the swings and had a good time.

It soaked them and the flowers. It also sprayed the dog, but not enough to scare it. The dog just shook its fur and wagged its tail. It thought they were playing with it.

Anna and Ben felt embarrassed. They looked silly and wet. They also felt sorry for the dog. They realized it was not mean. It was just curious and friendly. They turned off the hose and said sorry to the dog. The dog licked their faces and wagged its tail more. Anna and Ben smiled and petted the dog. They made a new friend.

The moral of the story is: Don't judge someone by their appearance. Sometimes they are nicer than they look. And don't use the hose to hurt someone. It can backfire and make you look foolish.

"No, let's try this way," Lily said, pointing to a path on the left.

"Fine, then. I'll go my way and you go yours. Bye, Tom!" Lily said, and ran to the left.

Then, they heard a voice. It was a tall man who worked in the park. He had a map of the maze and a whistle. He had heard their cries and came to help them.

"Hello, little ones. Are you lost?" he asked.

"Don't worry, don't worry. I'll help you. Blow this whistle and follow my voice. I'll guide you to the exit. And to each other," he said, giving them each a whistle.

"I'm sorry, Lily. I should have listened to you. I should have stayed with you," Tom said.

They thanked the tall man for helping them. He smiled and said, "You're welcome, little ones. I'm glad you're safe. But remember, next time, don't argue and don't split up. Stay together and work together. That's how you find the way out of any maze."

Tom and Lily nodded and said, "We will, sir. We will."

Tom and Mia were playing in the garden. They saw a big orange pumpkin on the ground. Tom wanted to touch it, but Mia said no.

"Why not?" Tom asked.

"Because it might be a sneezy pumpkin," Mia said.

"What is a sneezy pumpkin?" Tom wondered.

"A sneezy pumpkin is a pumpkin that makes you sneeze when you touch it. It is very silly and funny, but also very annoying," Mia explained.

Tom did not believe Mia. He thought she was making it up. He reached out his hand to touch the pumpkin. But as soon as he touched it, he felt a tickle in his nose. He sneezed so hard that he fell backwards.

"Achoo!" Tom sneezed.

"See? I told you it was a sneezy pumpkin," Mia said.

Tom rubbed his nose and looked at the pumpkin. He saw that it had a small hole on the side. He realized that it was not a real pumpkin, but a hollow one with some pepper inside. Someone had played a trick on them.

"Who did this?" Tom asked.

"I don't know. Maybe it was Sam. He likes to play jokes on us," Mia guessed.

Tom and Mia decided to find Sam and get him back. They picked up the sneezy pumpkin and carried it to Sam's house. They knocked on the door and waited. When Sam opened the door, they threw the sneezy pumpkin at him and ran away.

"Surprise!" Tom and Mia shouted.

Sam caught the sneezy pumpkin and looked at it. He felt a tickle in his nose. He sneezed so hard that he dropped the pumpkin.

"Achoo!" Sam sneezed.

Tom and Mia laughed and hid behind a bush. They thought it was a harmless joke. They did not know that Sam was allergic to pepper. He sneezed and sneezed and sneezed until his mom came and took him to the doctor.

Anna was a thoughtful girl who liked to help others. She often visited her grandma, who was old and used a cane to walk. Anna liked to talk to her grandma and listen to her stories.

One day, Anna saw a big bag of apples at the market. She thought they would make a nice gift for her grandma, who loved apples. She asked the seller how much they cost. The seller said they cost one coin for each apple.

Anna counted her coins. She had five coins. She could buy five apples, but the bag had more than five apples. She wanted to buy the whole bag for her grandma. She had an idea. She asked the seller if he had a scale to weigh the apples.

The seller nodded and brought out a scale. He put the bag of apples on one side and a weight on the other side. The scale balanced. He said the bag of apples weighed the same as the weight.

Anna looked at the weight. It had a number on it. The number was ten. Anna thought hard. She remembered that her grandma's cane also had a number on it. The number was ten. She wondered if her grandma's cane weighed the same as the bag of apples.

She asked the seller if he would trade the bag of apples for her grandma's cane. The seller was surprised, but he agreed. He gave Anna the bag of apples and took her grandma's cane.

Anna was happy. She ran to her grandma's house with the bag of apples. She knocked on the door and gave her grandma the bag of apples. She said she traded her grandma's cane for the apples.

Her grandma was shocked. She asked Anna why she did that. She said she needed her cane to walk. She said she could not walk without her cane.

Anna felt sad. She did not think of that. She wanted to make her grandma happy, but she made her unhappy. She said she was sorry. She said she would get her cane back.

She ran back to the market with the bag of apples. She looked for the seller, but he was gone. He had left with her grandma's cane. Anna cried. She did not know what to do.

A kind man saw Anna crying. He asked her what was wrong. Anna told him what happened. The kind man felt sorry for Anna. He said he had a spare cane at home. He said he would give it to Anna if she gave him the bag of apples.

Anna was grateful. She thanked the kind man and gave him the bag of apples. He gave her the spare cane. He said it was a good trade. He said he liked apples and he did not need two canes.

Anna smiled. She ran back to her grandma's house with the spare cane. She knocked on the door and gave her grandma the spare cane. She said she got it from a kind man who traded it for the bag of apples.

Her grandma was relieved. She hugged Anna and thanked her. She said she was proud of her. She said she was a thoughtful girl who learned from her mistake. She said she loved her.

Anna was happy. She hugged her grandma and said she loved her too. She said she learned a lesson. She said she would never trade something important for something less important. She said she would always think of the consequences of her actions.

The end.

"Oh no!" Ben cried. He got up and ran to the drain. He looked inside. The sack was gone. The water had taken it away.

"Ben, are you okay?" Lily asked. She came to the drain and looked too.

"I'm okay, but the sack is gone. The worms are gone. The drain took them away," Ben said. He felt sad.

"That's too bad," Lily said. She felt sad too.

They heard their mom calling them. They went to the house.

"Mom, we had a sack of worms, but we lost it in the drain," Ben said.

"A sack of worms? Why did you have a sack of worms?" Mom asked.

"We wanted to show you. We like worms. They are cool," Lily said.

Mom smiled. She hugged them.

"I'm sorry you lost your sack of worms, but I'm glad you're okay. Worms are cool, but they are also disgusting. They belong in the dirt, not in a sack. Next time, just show me one or two, okay?" Mom said.

"Okay, mom," Ben and Lily said.

They went inside and washed their hands. They decided to play with something else. They still liked worms, but they did not want to lose them in the drain again.

The moral of the story is: Do not play with matches. They are not toys. They are dangerous. Listen to your brother and your mommy. They love you and want you to be safe. Sharing is better than burning.

The butterfly remained there, watching and waiting. After a few days, the eggs began to move and crack. Suddenly, a small group of baby caterpillars came out of the eggs!

The butterfly stayed with the caterpillars, and watched them eat pieces of the flower and drink drops of morning dew. Over time, the caterpillars began to grow and change until finally, each one turned into the most beautiful butterfly!

The butterfly was so happy and proud that it had remained with the caterpillars to see them turn into butterflies. It flew away, celebrating its new friends, and the joy of being so curious!

The people in the city started to get angry. They shouted and pointed and told her to leave. Sarah was so scared and started to cry.

Suddenly, Sarah's mum came and put her arm around Sarah's shoulders. She said, "It's ok, Sarah. Let's go home now and you can have a little time out." 

From then on, Sarah remembered to always behave when she went to the city and she never forgot to be respectful to the people around her.

Lily liked to play in the garden with her mom. She saw many flowers and bugs. She saw a yellow and black bug that flew and made a buzz sound. She asked her mom, "What is that?"

Her mom said, "That is a bee. A bee is a bug that makes honey. Honey is sweet and good to eat. But you have to be careful. A bee can sting you if you touch it or make it angry. A sting hurts a lot."

Lily wanted to know more. She asked her mom, "Why does a bee make honey? How does it sting?"

Her mom said, "A bee makes honey by taking nectar from the flowers. Nectar is a juice that flowers have. A bee has a tongue that can suck the nectar. Then it takes the nectar to its home, which is called a hive. A hive is a house made of wax that many bees live in. In the hive, the bees turn the nectar into honey and store it in cells. Cells are small rooms in the hive. The bees use the honey for food when it is cold or dark outside."

Her mom said, "A bee can sting by using a sharp part in its back. This part is called a stinger. A bee only uses its stinger to protect itself or its hive. When a bee stings, it leaves its stinger in your skin. This makes the bee die. That is why a bee does not sting unless it has to. If you get stung by a bee, you have to take out the stinger and put some ice on it. Then it will feel better."

Lily said, "Thank you, mom. You explain very well. I like bees, but I will not touch them. I will watch them from far away. They are very busy and smart."

There was a king who had a big castle and many things. He liked to eat a lot of food every day, but he did not like to share with anyone. He was very greedy and selfish.

One day, a poor man came to his castle and asked for some bread. He was very hungry and had no home. The king said, "No, this is my food. Go away, you are dirty and ugly." The poor man said, "Please, kind king, have mercy on me. I only need a little bit of bread. You have so much, and I have nothing." The king said, "No, no, no. You are a liar and a thief. If you do not leave, I will call my guards and they will hurt you."

The poor man was very sad and scared. He turned to leave, but then he saw a big cake on the king's table. It looked so yummy and sweet. He thought, "Maybe I can take a small piece of cake. The king will not notice, and I will not be hungry anymore." He reached for the cake, but the king saw him and shouted, "Stop! How dare you touch my cake! You are a bad man and a robber. Guards, guards, catch him and throw him in the dungeon!"

The guards came and grabbed the poor man. They dragged him to the dungeon and locked him up. The poor man cried and prayed. He said, "Oh, God, please help me. I only wanted some food. I did not mean to steal. Forgive me for my mistake."

God heard his prayer and felt sorry for him. He decided to teach the king a lesson. He made the king very hungry, but no matter how much he ate, he was never full. He ate and ate and ate, but he still felt empty and weak. He also made the king very lonely, but no matter how many people he called, he was never happy. He quarreled and yelled and scolded, but he still felt angry and sad.

The king realized that he had been very wrong and wicked. He said, "Oh, God, please help me. I have been very greedy and selfish. I did not share with anyone. I treated the poor man very badly. Forgive me for my sins."

God heard his prayer and felt sorry for him. He said, "If you want to be forgiven, you must repent and change. You must share your food and your things with the poor and the needy. You must be kind and gentle with everyone. You must free the poor man from the dungeon and ask for his forgiveness."

The king agreed and did as God said. He shared his food and his things with the poor and the needy. He was kind and gentle with everyone. He freed the poor man from the dungeon and asked for his forgiveness. The poor man forgave him and thanked him. They became friends and ate the cake together.

The king learned his lesson and became a good and generous king. He was never hungry or lonely again. He was always full and happy. He thanked God for his mercy and grace.

The moral of the story is: Do not be greedy and selfish, but be generous and kind. Share what you have with others, and you will be blessed. Do not quarrel and yell, but be gentle and respectful. Treat others as you want to be treated, and you will have peace.

Sam looks at his toys. He has a blue truck, a yellow ball, and a green dinosaur. He thinks the green dinosaur is the best. He says, "I can trade you my green dinosaur. It is big and scary. It can roar and bite."

Ben likes the green dinosaur too. He says, "OK, that is a good trade. You can have my red car, and I can have your green dinosaur. But be careful, the red car is dangerous. It can go very fast and crash."

Sam nods. He takes the red car and gives Ben the green dinosaur. They start to play with their new toys. Sam makes the red car zoom and beep. Ben makes the green dinosaur growl and snap. They have a lot of fun. They are happy with their trade.

Mommy heard his cry and came running. She saw what had happened and was very angry. She scolded Timmy for being naughty and for taking the coin. She told him that the coin was not a toy, but a part of a science project. She also told him that copper can conduct electricity, and that he could have been hurt even more.

Timmy was very sorry and ashamed. He said he was sorry to Mommy and to the coin. He learned his lesson and never took things that were not his again. He also learned to be careful with copper and electricity. He hated the shock and the pain. He wanted to be a good boy.

Anna and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. They had a big box of blocks and they wanted to build a castle. Anna had an idea. She said, "Let's make a castle with a tower and a gate and a flag." Ben nodded and said, "Yes, let's do that."

They started to stack the blocks and make the walls of the castle. They used red blocks for the tower, blue blocks for the gate, and yellow blocks for the flag. They worked hard and had fun. They were very obedient and did not make a mess or fight.

But then, their little brother Tom came in. He saw the castle and he wanted to play too. He ran to the castle and tried to grab the flag. He pulled and pulled and the tower fell down. The blocks crashed and the castle was ruined. Anna and Ben were sad and angry. They shouted, "Tom, no! You broke our castle! Go away!"

Tom was scared and sorry. He did not mean to break the castle. He just wanted to join the game. He said, "I'm sorry, Anna and Ben. I did not mean to break your castle. Please, can I play with you? Please, can we build the castle again?"

Anna and Ben looked at Tom. They saw that he was sorry and that he wanted to play. They decided to forgive him and let him play. They said, "OK, Tom. You can play with us. But you have to be obedient and careful. You have to listen to us and not break the castle. Do you understand?"

Tom nodded and said, "Yes, I understand. I will be obedient and careful. I will listen to you and not break the castle. Thank you, Anna and Ben."

They smiled and hugged Tom. Then they picked up the blocks and started to build the castle again. They helped each other and shared the blocks. They made a bigger and better castle than before. They had a lot of fun and they were happy.

Lily and Ben were playing in the kitchen. They liked to pretend they were chefs and make yummy food. They used pots and pans and spoons and bowls. They also used some things from the cupboard, like flour and sugar and salt.

"Look, I made a cake!" Lily said, holding up a plate with a messy pile of flour and sugar. "Do you want some?"

"No, thank you," Ben said. "I made soup. It has salt and water and carrots. It is very good. You can have some of my soup."

Lily looked at Ben's soup. It was in a big pot on the stove. It smelled nice. She wanted to try some. She put down her plate and went to the stove.

"Hey, that's mine!" Ben shouted. "You can't have my soup! You have your own cake!"

"But I want some soup too!" Lily said. "It's not fair that you have soup and I have cake. Cake is not good for lunch. Soup is better. Let me have some!"

She reached for the pot, but Ben pushed her away. He was angry. He did not want to share his soup. He wanted it all for himself.

Lily fell to the floor. She hit her head on the corner of the cupboard. It hurt a lot. She started to cry. Blood came out of her head. It made a big stain on the floor.

Ben saw the blood. He was scared. He did not mean to hurt Lily. He just wanted his soup. He ran to the door and called for Mom.

"Mom, Mom, come quick!" he yelled. "Lily is hurt! She has blood on her head! I pushed her and she fell!"

Mom came running. She saw Lily on the floor. She saw the blood. She saw the pot of soup and the plate of cake. She was very angry and very sad.

She picked up Lily and hugged her. She took her to the car and drove to the hospital. She did not say a word to Ben. She left him alone in the kitchen. He felt very bad. He wished he had shared his soup with Lily. He wished he had not pushed her. He wished he had been a good brother. He wished he could say sorry. But it was too late.

Ben and Lily were playing in the park. They saw a big hole in the ground. It was a pit. They wanted to see what was inside.

"Let's go down the pit," Ben said. "Maybe we can find something cool."

"No, Ben, that's not safe," Lily said. "The pit is deep and dark. We might get hurt or lost."

But Ben did not listen. He jumped into the pit. He landed on something soft and squishy. It was a pile of rotten apples.

"Yuck!" Ben said. "This is gross. And it smells bad. Help me, Lily!"

Lily was scared. She did not know how to help Ben. She ran to find a grown-up. She saw a man with a hat and a shovel. He was a gardener.

"Please, sir, help me," Lily said. "My friend is in the pit. He jumped in and he can't get out."

The gardener followed Lily to the pit. He saw Ben covered in rotten apples. He shook his head.

"That was a silly thing to do, boy," he said. "You could have been hurt. Or worse. You should listen to your friend. She is smart and careful."

He used his shovel to make a ladder out of dirt. He helped Ben climb out of the pit. Ben was dizzy and dirty. He felt sick.

"Thank you, sir," Ben said. "I'm sorry, Lily. You were right. The pit was not fun. It was dangerous. I should have listened to you."

Lily hugged Ben. She was glad he was safe. She forgave him.

The gardener smiled. He was proud of Lily. He applauded her.

"Good job, Lily," he said. "You are a good friend. And a brave girl. You did the right thing. You asked for help. And you learned a lesson. Never go into a pit. It's not worth it."

Ben and Lily nodded. They learned their lesson. They thanked the gardener again. They went home. They never played in the pit again. They played in the sandbox instead. It was much more fun. And much safer.

Lily and Ben were friends who liked to play outside. One day, they decided to go for a walk in the valley near their home. The valley was big and green, with many flowers and trees. They saw some birds and rabbits, and heard a stream.

"Look, Ben, there is a bridge over the stream!" Lily said. "Let's go and see what is on the other side."

"OK, Lily, but be careful. The bridge looks old and weak," Ben said.

They walked on the bridge, holding hands. But when they were in the middle, the bridge made a loud crack and broke. Lily and Ben fell into the water, which was cold and fast.

"Help, help!" they cried. "We can't swim!"

A man who was working in the field heard their cries. He ran to the stream and saw the two children in the water. He threw a rope to them and pulled them out. He wrapped them in a warm blanket and took them to his house.

"Thank you, thank you, sir, for saving us!" Lily and Ben said.

"You're welcome, children. I'm glad you're safe. But you shouldn't have crossed that bridge. It was old and empty. No one uses it anymore. It's dangerous," the man said.

"We're sorry, sir. We didn't know. We just wanted to see what was on the other side of the valley," Lily and Ben said.

"Well, now you know. There is nothing on the other side of the valley. It's empty and lonely. The only thing you'll find there is trouble. You should stay on this side, where there are people and animals and plants. That's where you belong," the man said.

Lily and Ben nodded. They learned their lesson. They thanked the man again and went back to their home. They never crossed the bridge again. They played in the valley, where they were happy and safe.

"I want to reach the top," said the spider. "I know I can do it!"

The little spider kept going. He twisted around the branches and leaves. He did not give up. He was a very persistent spider. Finally, he reached the top of the tree.

The little spider looked down and saw his friend, the bird. "I did it!" he called out. "I made it to the top!"

The bird smiled and said, "You are a very brave and persistent spider. Well done!"

Finally, a little boy came up to the mule and started to pet it gently. The mule liked the boy and followed him around. The farmer was amazed and decided to sell the mule to the boy for a lower price. From then on, the mule was happy and the boy had a new friend. The end.

Jack had never tasted an onion before, but he was quite brave. With a little encouragement from his mommy, he took a bite. It was crunchy, and a little spicy, but Jack liked it! 

Since then, Jack has always looked forward to picnics at the park. And his mommy always suggests adding an onion to the picnic basket.

The little girl smiled and started to spin her own top. It was bright pink with a wooden handle. She was so lost in her own spinning that she didn't realize that the woman had stopped to watch her.

Finally, the woman smiled and said, "I recognize your top. I used to play with one just like it when I was small. I am very pleased to see you enjoying the same game I did."

The little girl was delighted. She smiled back at the woman and thanked her for the kind words. They said goodbye and both continued on their way, each spinning their own top with a smile of recognition.

Lila was a very independent cat. She liked to do things by herself, without any help from her humans. She did not like to wear a collar, or to sleep in a basket, or to play with toys. She liked to explore the garden, and to hunt for mice, and to nap in the sun.

She jumped up and tried to open it, but it was too hard. She scratched and bit the can, but it did not open. She was very frustrated and hungry.

Then she heard a voice. It was her human, Emma. Emma saw Lila on the counter, and smiled. She said, "Lila, do you want some tuna?" She took the can and opened it with a tool. She put some tuna in a bowl and put it on the floor. She said, "Here you go, Lila. Enjoy your tuna."

Lila looked at the bowl and then at Emma. She was tempted by the tuna, but she did not want to seem too eager. She wanted to show Emma that she was independent, and that she did not need her. She pretended to ignore the bowl and the human. She walked away from the counter and jumped on the sofa. She lay down and licked her paw.

Emma was not fooled by Lila's act. She knew that Lila was proud and stubborn, but also curious and smart. She decided to try a different approach. Lila watched Emma from the sofa. She smelled the tuna again, and felt her mouth water. She wondered what it would be like to share some tuna with Emma. She thought that maybe Emma was not so bad, and that maybe she could be her friend. She decided to give it a try. She got off the sofa and walked slowly to Emma. She kneel down next to her and sniffed the bowl. She licked some tuna and said, "Meow."

Emma smiled and said, "Good girl, Lila. I'm glad you like it." She stroked Lila's fur and said, "You are a very independent cat, but you can also be a very sweet cat. I love you, Lila." She gave Lila a kiss and said, "Let's eat some tuna together, okay?"

Lila purred and said, "Meow." She ate some more tuna and rubbed her head against Emma's leg. She felt happy and warm. She thought that maybe being independent was good, but being loved was better. She thought that maybe she could have both. She thought that maybe she and Emma could be a family.

That night, Lily went to bed and felt something crawling on her leg. She screamed and her mom came running. They found the spider had crawled into Lily's bed because of all the toys on the floor. From that day on, Lily always made sure to clean up her toys before going to bed, so she wouldn't have any more scary surprises.

One day, her friend Ben came to play with her. Ben saw her novels and wanted to read one. He asked Lily, "Can I read one of your novels, please?"

Lily said, "No, they are mine. You cannot read them. Go away."

Ben was sad. He said, "But I like novels too. Why are you so selfish? Sharing is good. Don't you want to be my friend?"

Lily did not care. She said, "I don't need friends. I have my novels. They are more fun than you. Leave me alone."

Ben left. He did not want to play with Lily anymore. He hoped to find a better friend. A friend who was kind and generous. A friend who liked to share.

Lily stayed in her room. She read her novels. She was alone. She did not have any friends. She was not happy. She realized that she was wrong. She wished she had shared her novels with Ben. She wished she had been his friend. She hoped he would forgive her.

The moral of the story is: Don't be selfish. Share what you have with others. Friends are more important than things.

Tom was a cricket who liked to drink juice. He lived in a big garden with many flowers and fruits. Every day, he would hop from one plant to another and sip the sweet juice from the petals and the seeds.

One day, he saw a new fruit that he had never seen before. It was round and red and shiny. It looked delicious. Tom wanted to try it. He hopped closer and closer to the fruit, until he reached it. He bit a small piece and tasted it. It was very sour and bitter. Tom did not like it at all. He spat it out and made a face.

Suddenly, he heard a loud noise. It was a bird who had seen him. The bird wanted to eat him. Tom was scared. He tried to run away, but the bird was faster. It flew towards him and opened its big beak.

Tom thought he was going to be eaten. He closed his eyes and waited. But then, he felt something wet and sticky on his back. It was juice. The fruit that he had bitten had squirted juice on him. The juice was sour and bitter for Tom, but it was also sour and bitter for the bird. The bird did not like it either. It spat out Tom and flew away.

Tom was safe. He was also very wet and sticky. He looked for a place to clean himself. He saw a pond nearby. He hopped to the pond and dipped himself in the water. The water was cool and fresh. Tom drank some of the water. It was delicious. He felt happy and thirsty. He drank more and more water, until he was full and clean.

Tom learned a lesson that day. He learned that not all fruits are good to drink. He also learned that sometimes, water is the best drink of all. He decided to stick to the flowers and the seeds that he knew and liked. He also decided to be more careful of birds and other dangers. He thanked the fruit for saving him, even though it was sour and bitter. He hoped that the bird would find something else to eat, something that was delicious for it. He hopped away, looking for his friends. He wanted to tell them his story.

One day, they heard a loud noise from the other room. It sounded like a monster, roaring and banging. They were scared. They stopped playing and looked at each other.

"What is that?" Tim asked.

"I don't know," Lily said. "Maybe it's a dragon, or a giant, or a ghost."

They hugged their boat and moved closer to the door. They wanted to run away, but they were too afraid to move.

The noise came closer and closer. They heard footsteps and breathing. They closed their eyes and hoped it would go away.

Suddenly, the door opened. They saw a big shadow on the wall. They screamed.

"Ahoy, mateys!" a voice said. "What are you doing here?"

They opened their eyes and saw their dad. He was wearing a funny hat and a coat. He had a broom in his hand. He smiled and winked at them.

"Dad!" they cried. "You scared us!"

"Sorry, kids," he said. "I was just cleaning the garage. I found this old costume and I thought I would surprise you. Do you want to play pirates with me?"

They looked at each other and nodded. They were not scared anymore. They were happy.

They gave their dad their boat and followed him to the tub. They sailed their boat and had fun. They forgot about the monster noise. They only heard their dad's silly pirate talk. They laughed and played until it was time for dinner.

Sara did not like broccoli. She thought it was ugly and green and yucky. She did not want to eat it for dinner. She wanted to eat cake and ice cream instead.

But Mom said no. Mom said she had to eat her broccoli first. Mom said broccoli was good for her and made her strong and healthy. Mom said cake and ice cream were only for special days.

Sara was sad and angry. She did not want to be strong and healthy. She wanted to be happy and sweet. She looked at her plate and saw the ugly broccoli. She made a face and pushed it away.

Then she had an idea. She saw her dog, Spot, under the table. Spot liked to eat anything. Maybe Spot would eat her broccoli for her. Then she could have cake and ice cream.

She picked up a piece of broccoli and threw it to Spot. Spot caught it in his mouth and wagged his tail. Sara smiled and threw another piece. Spot ate it too. Sara was happy. She thought she was very clever.

But Mom saw what Sara was doing. Mom was not happy. Mom said Sara was not allowed to feed Spot her broccoli. Mom said Spot could get sick from eating too much broccoli. Mom said Sara had to eat her broccoli herself.

Sara was sad and angry again. She did not want to eat her broccoli. She did not want to make Spot sick. She did not want to make Mom unhappy. She did not know what to do.

Then Spot did something funny. He burped. He burped very loud and very long. He burped so loud and so long that Sara and Mom and Dad and even the cat laughed. They laughed so hard that they forgot about the broccoli.

Sara was happy again. She thought Spot was very funny. She gave him a hug and a kiss. She said she was sorry for giving him her broccoli. She said she loved him very much.

Mom was happy too. She said she was sorry for being mad at Sara. She said she loved her very much. She said she could have a little cake and ice cream if she ate some of her broccoli.

Sara agreed. She ate some of her broccoli. She did not like it, but she did not make a face. She said it was not so bad. She said she wanted to be strong and healthy like Mom.

Then she had some cake and ice cream. She liked it very much. She said it was very good. She said she wanted to be happy and sweet like Dad.

They all had a good dinner. They all said thank you and good night. They all went to bed. They all dreamed of broccoli and cake and ice cream and Spot. They all were happy. The end.

Tom was a boy who liked to make noise. He had a toy drum, a toy guitar and a toy trumpet. He played them all day and all night. His mom and dad did not like the noise. They said, "Tom, please play quietly. You are making our ears hurt."

One day, Tom saw a big brown dog in the park. The dog was barking loudly. Tom thought the dog was funny. He wanted to play with the dog. He ran to the dog with his toy trumpet. He blew the trumpet in the dog's face. The dog did not like the trumpet. The dog growled and showed his teeth.

"Tom, stop that! You are making the dog angry!" his mom shouted. But Tom did not listen. He blew the trumpet louder and louder. The dog barked louder and louder. The dog jumped at Tom and bit his trumpet. The trumpet broke in half. Tom was scared and sad. He dropped the trumpet and ran to his mom.

"Mom, the dog broke my trumpet!" he cried.

Sara liked to read novels. Novels were books with many words and pictures that told stories. Sara had many novels in her room. She liked to read them before she slept.

One day, Sara found a novel she had never seen before. It was about a bird that could soar in the sky. Soar meant to fly very high and fast. Sara wanted to soar like the bird. She opened the novel and started to read.

The bird in the novel was very flexible. Flexible meant to bend and twist easily. The bird could fly in different ways and do tricks in the air. The bird had many friends who liked to watch him soar. The bird was happy.

But one day, the bird met a hawk. A hawk was a big and strong bird that liked to eat other birds. The hawk saw the bird and wanted to catch him. The bird tried to soar away, but the hawk was faster. The bird was scared.

"Help me, please!" the bird cried. "Is anyone there?"

Sara heard the bird's cry. She felt sorry for the bird. She wanted to help him. She closed her eyes and wished very hard. She wished she could soar like the bird and save him from the hawk.

Suddenly, Sara felt a strange feeling. She opened her eyes and saw that she was no longer in her room. She was in the sky, next to the bird. She had wings and feathers. She had become a bird!

"Wow!" Sara said. "I can soar!"

"Thank you for coming!" the bird said. "You are very kind. Can you help me escape from the hawk?"

"Yes, I can!" Sara said. "Follow me!"

Sara and the bird soared together. They used their flexible wings to dodge and weave. They flew higher and lower, faster and slower. They confused the hawk and made him tired. The hawk gave up and flew away.

"Yay! We did it!" Sara and the bird cheered. "We are safe!"

"You are amazing!" the bird said. "You can soar better than anyone I know. How did you do it?"

"I don't know," Sara said. "I just wished very hard. I wanted to soar like you and help you. I like your novel. It is very exciting."

"Thank you," the bird said. "You are very brave and generous. You are my friend. Do you want to stay with me and soar some more?"

Sara thought for a moment. She liked to soar with the bird. It was fun and beautiful. But she also missed her home and her family. She missed her other novels and her bed. She had to go back.

"I'm sorry," Sara said. "I can't stay. I have to go home. But I will always remember you and our adventure. Maybe we can meet again someday."

"OK," the bird said. "I understand. I will miss you. But I will always remember you too. You are the best friend I ever had. Goodbye, Sara."

"Goodbye, bird," Sara said.

Sara closed her eyes and wished very hard. She wished she could go back to her room and her normal life. She felt a strange feeling. She opened her eyes and saw that she was in her bed, holding the novel. She was a girl again.

She smiled and hugged the novel. She was happy. She had learned something new. She had learned that reading novels can make you soar in your imagination. She had learned that being flexible can help you overcome challenges. She had learned that being kind and helpful can make you friends. She had learned a lot from the novel.

She put the novel on her shelf and turned off the light. She closed her eyes and fell asleep. She dreamed of soaring with the bird. She dreamed of novels. She dreamed of being flexible, kind and helpful. She dreamed of being happy.

Tom liked to eat pasta with sauce. He liked red sauce and green sauce and white sauce. He liked to put a lot of sauce on his pasta and make it very wet.

One day, Tom went to a restaurant with his mom and dad. He saw pasta with sauce on the menu and he wanted it. He asked his mom to order it for him. She said yes and told the waiter.

When the pasta came, Tom was very happy. He took a big fork and put some pasta in his mouth. But the sauce was very hot and spicy. It made his tongue burn and his eyes water. He spit out the pasta and cried. He wanted water and milk and bread.

The waiter and the other people in the restaurant looked at Tom. They saw the sauce on his face and his shirt and his plate. They heard him cry and saw him spit. Some of them laughed and some of them said "aww". Tom felt very embarrassed. He wished he had ordered something else.

His mom and dad hugged him and gave him water and milk and bread. They told him it was okay and they were sorry. They asked the waiter to bring him another pasta with a different sauce. They said they would help him clean his face and his shirt and his plate. They said they loved him and he was a good boy.

Tom felt a little better. He said he was sorry and he loved them too. He tried the new pasta with a different sauce. It was not hot and spicy. It was sweet and creamy. He liked it and ate it. He was not embarrassed anymore. He was happy and full.

Ben and Lily went to the park with Mom. They saw a pond with many ducks. The ducks were light brown and white. They had yellow beaks and feet. Ben and Lily liked the ducks. They wanted to feed them bread.

"Mom, can we give bread to the ducks?" Ben asked.

"Sure, but only a little bit. Too much bread is not good for them," Mom said. She gave them some bread pieces.

Ben and Lily threw the bread into the pond. The ducks swam to get the bread. They quacked and splashed. Ben and Lily laughed. They liked to watch the ducks.

One duck was different from the others. It was bigger and darker. It had a red head and a blue wing. It did not eat the bread. It acted funny. It made loud noises and chased the other ducks. It scared them away.

"Look, Mom, that duck is acting bad. Why is it so mean?" Lily asked.

"That's not a duck, sweetie. That's a goose. Geese are different from ducks. They are more aggressive and territorial. They don't like to share," Mom explained.

"Can we make it go away?" Ben asked.

"No, we can't. We have to respect its space. Let's leave the pond and go to the playground. Maybe we can see some nice ducks there," Mom suggested.

Ben and Lily agreed. They said goodbye to the ducks and the goose. They went to the playground. They had fun on the swings and the slide. They forgot about the mean goose. They were happy.

Lily and Tom were friends. They liked to play in the snow. One day, they saw a big snowman in the park. He had a hat, a scarf, a carrot nose and two eyes made of coal.

"Hello, snowman!" Lily said. "Do you want to play with us?"

The snowman did not say anything. He just looked at them with his coal eyes.

"Maybe he is hungry," Tom said. "Let's feed him something."

They looked around and saw a bakery. They ran inside and bought a tasty cake. They brought it back to the snowman.

"Here you go, snowman," Tom said. "This is for you. It is very tasty."

They put the cake in front of the snowman's mouth. But the snowman did not eat it. He just looked at them with his coal eyes.

"Maybe he does not like cake," Lily said. "Maybe he likes something else."

They looked around and saw a bird feeder. They ran to it and took some seeds. They brought them back to the snowman.

"Here you go, snowman," Lily said. "This is for you. It is very tasty."

They put the seeds in front of the snowman's mouth. But the snowman did not eat them. He just looked at them with his coal eyes.

"Maybe he does not like seeds," Tom said. "Maybe he likes something else."

They looked around and saw a pile of coal. They ran to it and took some pieces. They brought them back to the snowman.

"Here you go, snowman," Tom said. "This is for you. It is very tasty."

They put the coal in front of the snowman's mouth. But the snowman did not eat them. He just looked at them with his coal eyes.

Then, he opened his mouth and said, "No, thank you. I do not like coal. I like cake and seeds. But you took them all. That was not nice. Now I am angry."

He took off his hat and scarf and threw them at Lily and Tom. He took out his carrot nose and his coal eyes and threw them at Lily and Tom. He started to roll down the hill, chasing Lily and Tom.

"Run, run!" Lily and Tom shouted. "The snowman is mad at us!"

They ran away from the snowman as fast as they could. They learned a lesson. They should not take things that are not theirs. They should share and be kind.
