One day, she went to the library with her mom. She saw a big book with a colorful cover. It had a picture of a cat and a hat. She wanted to read it. She asked her mom, "Can I borrow this book?"

Her mom looked at the book. She smiled and said, "Sure, you can borrow this book. It is a very unusual book. It is a book of poems by Dr. Seuss. He was a funny man who wrote silly poems. Do you want to hear one?"

Lily nodded. She was curious. Her mom opened the book and read:

"The sun did not shine. It was too wet to play. So we sat in the house. All that cold, cold, wet day.

I sat there with Sally. We sat there, we two. And I said, 'How I wish we had something to do!'"

Lily giggled. She liked the rhyme. She liked the sound of the words. She wanted to hear more. She asked her mom, "Can you read another one?"

Her mom said, "Of course, I can read another one. How about this one?"

She turned the page and read:

"One fish, two fish, red fish, blue fish. Black fish, blue fish, old fish, new fish.

This one has a little star. This one has a little car. Say! What a lot of fish there are."

Lily clapped her hands. She liked the fish. She liked the colors. She liked the poem. She said, "This is a fun book. I want to borrow it. Can we take it home?"

Her mom said, "Yes, we can take it home. But we have to return it later. That is what borrowing means. You can use something for a while, but then you have to give it back. Do you understand?"

Lily nodded. She understood. She was happy. She hugged the book and said, "Thank you, mom. Thank you, Dr. Seuss. You made a very unusual book. A book of poems that I like."

Max asked his friend, the cow, "Can you help me split the fruit?" The cow tried to split the fruit with her hoof, but it did not break. Then, Max asked the sheep for help. The sheep tried to split the fruit by hitting it with her head, but it did not break.

Finally, Max asked his friend, the strong pig, to help. The pig used his strong nose and split the fruit into pieces. Max and his friends were very happy. They all shared the fruit and enjoyed eating it together.

Kim pushed the raft into the water and jumped on it. Tim followed her, but he felt afraid. He wished they had stayed at home.

They paddled hard, but the river was stronger. It made big waves that splashed them and pushed them around. The raft rocked and creaked. Tim and Kim held on tight, but they were wet and cold.

"Kim, this was a bad idea," Tim said. "We should go back. The storm is getting worse."

"No, we can make it," Kim said. "Look, there is Sam's house. We are almost there."

But as she said that, a big wave hit the raft and broke it in half. Tim and Kim screamed and fell into the water. They tried to swim, but the current was too fast. They were in trouble.

Sam heard their screams and ran out of his house. He saw them in the water and ran to his boat. He grabbed a rope and threw it to them.

"Tim, Kim, grab the rope!" he shouted. "I'll pull you in."

Tim and Kim saw the rope and reached for it. They were glad to see Sam. He was a good friend. He saved them from the river.

They got into the boat and hugged Sam. They were safe and happy.

"Thank you, Sam," Tim said. "You are a hero."

"Thank you, Sam," Kim said. "You are a hero. And I'm sorry. I was wrong. We should not have come today. It was too dangerous."

"That's okay," Sam said. "I'm just glad you are okay. And I have something to show you. A new toy. It's a radio. We can use it to talk to each other, even when we are far away. Next time, we can visit without the raft. And without the storm."

His mom and dad turned to him and frowned. They did not look happy and calm anymore.

"Ben, you know you have to sleep in your crib. You are a big boy now. You need to learn to sleep by yourself. It's good for you. We love you, but you have to respect our space and our rules. Go back to your crib, please." His dad said in a firm voice.

Ben felt ashamed. He knew he had done something wrong. He had disturbed his mom and dad's time together. He had disobeyed their rules. He had been selfish and sneaky. He hung his head and nodded.

"Okay, dad. I'm sorry, mom. I love you." He said in a soft voice.

He turned around and walked back to his crib. He climbed in and pulled the blanket over him. He felt sad and lonely. He wished he could sleep with his mom and dad.

But then he remembered what his dad had said. He was a big boy now. He needed to learn to sleep by himself. It was good for him. His mom and dad loved him, but they also needed their space and their rules. He had to respect them.

He closed his eyes and tried to think of happy things. He thought of his toys, his friends, his pets, his books. He thought of how his mom and dad would hug him and kiss him in the morning. He thought of how proud they would be of him for sleeping in his crib.

He felt a little better. He smiled and fell asleep.

The moral of the story is: Respect your parents' space and rules, and learn to be independent.

"Oh no, look at all the damage," she said.

"What's wrong, Tim?" Sam asked.

Suddenly, the little boy spotted his tire under a big bush. He was so happy and ran over to get it. However, he was so foolish and did not realize that the bush was full of sharp thorns. As soon as he tried to reach for the tire, he got scratched by the thorns.

His mom saw what happened and quickly ran to his side. She hugged him and gave him some ointment to reduce the pain. After applying the ointment, the little boy was feeling much better and he smiled again. From that moment on, he learned to be a bit more careful and always check for bushes.

But the shopkeeper had an idea. He asked Jack if he was a good helper. Jack nodded yes. So, the shopkeeper told Jack he could help him with some jobs around the shop. If he worked hard and helped with all the jobs, he could have an ice cream cone for free!

Jack was so excited! He worked hard all morning, helping the shopkeeper. When the jobs were done, the shopkeeper said, "Thank you for all your help Jack! You can have your ice cream cone now."

Jack was so happy! He waved goodbye to the shopkeeper, licking his delicious ice cream cone, and he ran happily back home.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Pete who liked to play in the rain. One day it was raining quite hard outside so Pete took out his umbrella and went for a walk. As he was walking, he stepped in a huge puddle and his feet got soaked! Pete was feeling helpless because the puddle was too deep to measure and he didn't know what to do. 

He ran back home as fast as he could and when his mom saw him, she knew she had to help. She took out a big towel and rubbed it against his feet. Pete's mom said, "Let's see if your shoes will dry or we'll have to find a way to soak the water out." She brought out a deep bowl of warm water, poured some baking soda in it and then put Pete's shoes in the bowl.

Pete said, "Mommy, what are you doing?" 

"I'm going to soak up the water inside the shoes," his mom replied. Sure enough, after an hour or two his shoes were as dry as a desert! Pete thanked his mom for her help, put on his now-dry shoes and walked off feeling much better.

The man went into the pond and retrieved the cap for Lily. She was so happy and grateful that she gave him a big hug. From that day on, Lily made sure to hold onto her cap tightly and always thanked the man who helped her.

"Yes, but we need to attach it to a string so you don't lose it," her mom replied.

Lily was happy and they attached the rock to a string. As they were walking home, they saw a deaf man crossing the street. Lily wanted to say hello, but her mom told her that the man couldn't hear her.

Suddenly, a car came speeding down the road and hit the man. Lily was very scared and started to cry. Her mom called for help, but it was too late. The man had died. Lily was sad that she couldn't say hello to him and the rock didn't make her happy anymore.

Benny continued his walk and saw a big rock. He tried to lift it, but it was too heavy. Benny thought, "I wonder how much this rock weighs?" 

After his walk, Benny went back to his cabin. He felt tired and decided to take a nap. As he slept, he dreamed of all the things he could weigh and how heavy they might be.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in the forest near her house. One day, she saw an owl sitting on a tree branch. The owl had big eyes and feathers that were as soft as a blanket. Lily felt happy to see the owl.

As she continued to play, she heard a loud noise. It was a strong wind that was blowing through the trees. The wind was so strong that it made the leaves on the trees shake. Lily felt scared because she had never felt such a strong wind before.

Suddenly, the owl flew down from the tree branch and landed on Lily's shoulder. The owl's feathers felt soft and warm, and Lily felt safe. The owl stayed with her until the wind stopped blowing. From that day on, Lily knew that whenever she felt scared or weak, the owl would be there to make her feel strong and safe again.

When Blue came back with the fuel, Red was so happy and thanked Blue. Red filled up his tank and they rushed to the park together. Red's friends were so happy to see him and they all had a great time playing together. From that day on, Red knew that his friends were always there to help him when he needed it.

Lily and Tom smile. They hold the lion's paw. They run out of the tent. They go to the zoo. They find the lion's family. They say goodbye to the lion. The lion says, "Goodbye, Lily and Tom. You are my heroes. You are my friends. I will never forget you."

Lily and Tom wave. They go back to the park. They are happy. They are proud. They are friends.

It is disgusting and dangerous. You can hurt yourself and others. You can make them sick or sad. You should say sorry and stop biting."

But then, something happened. Lily felt a sharp pain in her mouth. She looked at her teeth and saw that they were broken and bleeding. She had bitten too hard and too much. She had hurt herself. She felt scared and sorry. She wanted to stop biting.

She ran to Mr. Fox and said, "Mr. Fox, I'm sorry. I'm sorry for biting you and Ben and everything. I was wrong. Biting is not fun or funny. It is disgusting and dangerous. I don't want to bite anymore. Please help me."

Mr. Fox smiled and hugged Lily. He said, "Lily, I'm glad you realized your mistake. I forgive you. I will help you. I will teach you how to be kind and gentle. How to use your words and your hands. How to make friends and have fun. Biting is not the way. Loving is the way."

Lily nodded and smiled. She felt better and happier. She said, "Thank you, Mr. Fox. You are a good teacher. I will listen to you. I will not bite anymore. I will love instead."

"Wow, look at our ice-cream! It's glowing!" Lily said.

"I don't like it either! It's gross!" Ben said.

One day, a man wanted to record a song. He had a big box that could make sounds and a small stick that could catch his voice. He liked to sing and play with the box and the stick. He wanted to share his song with other people.

He went to a place where there were many houses and people. He looked for a good spot to record his song. He saw a big tree with a lot of birds. He thought the birds would make his song more pretty. He put his box and his stick under the tree and started to sing.

But the birds did not like his song. They thought he was too loud and noisy. They started to peck at his box and his stick. They made his song sound bad. The man was sad and angry. He tried to shoo the birds away, but they did not listen. They kept pecking and squawking.

The man gave up. He picked up his box and his stick and ran away. He looked for another place to record his song. He saw a hill with a lot of flowers. He thought the flowers would make his song more sweet. He put his box and his stick on the hill and started to sing.

But the flowers did not like his song. They thought he was too hot and dry. They started to wilt and droop. They made his song look sad. The man was confused and sorry. He tried to water the flowers, but they did not perk up. They kept wilting and drooping.

The man gave up. He picked up his box and his stick and ran away. He looked for another place to record his song. He saw a lake with a lot of fish. He thought the fish would make his song more fun. He put his box and his stick by the lake and started to sing.

But the fish did not like his song. They thought he was too strange and scary. They started to splash and jump. They made his song wet and messy. The man was surprised and wet. He tried to dry his box and his stick, but they did not work. They were broken and silent.

The man gave up. He picked up his box and his stick and ran away. He did not want to record his song anymore. He felt alone and sad. He did not know where to go.

He saw a distant house with a lot of lights. He thought maybe someone would like his song. He walked to the house and knocked on the door. A woman opened the door and smiled at him. She asked him who he was and what he wanted.

The man told her his name and his story. He showed her his box and his stick. He asked her if she would like to hear his song. The woman nodded and invited him in. She had a big couch and a warm fire. She had a new box and a new stick. She said she liked to record songs too. She said they could record a song together.

The man was happy and grateful. He thanked the woman and sat on the couch. He took the new box and the new stick and started to sing. The woman joined him and sang along. They made a beautiful song. They recorded it and played it back. They smiled and hugged. They became friends.

One night, he sneaked into the kitchen and took a big bag of candy from the cupboard. He ran to his room and locked the door. He opened the bag and started to eat the candy. He ate and ate and ate, until he felt sick. He threw the bag on the floor and lay on his bed.

He heard a knock on the door. It was his mom. She said, "Timmy, open the door. I know you have candy in there. You have to share with your sister. She has no candy and she is sad."

Timmy did not want to share. He said, "Go away, mom. I hate you. I hate my sister. This is my candy and I will eat it all."

He heard another knock on the door. It was not his mom. It was a scary voice. It said, "Timmy, open the door. I know you have candy in there. You have to share with me. I have no candy and I am hungry."

Timmy was afraid. He said, "Who are you? Go away. This is my candy and I will eat it all."

Timmy screamed. He threw his candy at the skeleton. He said, "Take it, take it. I don't want it anymore. Please don't eat me. I'm sorry, I'm sorry."

The skeleton laughed. It said, "Too late, Timmy. You have been very bad. You have not shared your candy with anyone. You have not listened to your mom. You have not loved your sister. You have only loved yourself. And now you will pay. You will become a candy skeleton like me."

The skeleton grabbed Timmy and bit him. Timmy felt a sharp pain. He looked at his arm and saw that it was turning into candy. He cried and cried, but no one heard him. The skeleton ate him until there was nothing left but bones and teeth. Then it took the bag of candy and left.

One evening, she looked out of her window and saw the sunset. It was very pretty. It had many colors. She remembered how she and Ben used to watch the sunset together and say how sweet it was. She missed Ben. She realized she had made a mistake. She felt sorry.

She decided to take the sack back to the park and look for Ben. She hoped he would forgive her. She hoped they could be friends again. She hoped they could watch the sunset together and say how sweet it was.

The moral of the story is: Do not be selfish and take what is not yours. Be honest and kind. Friendship is more important than toys.

"Oh no," Ben said. "We broke the window and lost the baseball. What will we do?"

Sam and Mia are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big tap near the pond. The tap is shiny and has a red handle.

"Look, a tap!" Sam says. "I want to turn it on and see what happens."

"Me too!" Mia says. "Let's go and try it."

Sam and Mia run to the tap. Sam gets there first. He grabs the handle and tries to turn it. But it is too hard. He cannot move it.

"Let me try!" Mia says. She pushes Sam away and holds the handle. She pulls and pulls. But she cannot move it either.

"It's not fair!" Sam says. "You pushed me. I want to try again."

"No, it's my turn!" Mia says. "You had your chance. I want to try more."

Sam and Mia start to argue. They pull and tug at the handle. They shout and cry. They forget to have fun.

A man sees them. He works in the park. He knows how to use the tap. He walks over to them.

"Hello, children," he says. "What are you doing?"

"We want to turn on the tap," Sam says.

"But we can't," Mia says.

The man smiles. He says, "The tap is not for playing. It is for watering the flowers. It is very hard to turn on. You need a special key. I have the key. Do you want to see?"

Sam and Mia nod. They stop arguing. They are curious.

The man takes out a small key from his pocket. He puts it in a hole on the tap. He turns the key. Then he turns the handle. The tap makes a noise. Water comes out of the tap. It makes a fountain. The water is cold and clear.

"Wow!" Sam and Mia say. They clap their hands. They laugh. They run under the water. They get wet and happy.

The man says, "Do you want to help me water the flowers? You can lead the water with this hose. It is like a snake. You can make it go where you want."

Sam and Mia say, "Yes, please!" They take the hose. They lead the water to the flowers. The flowers are colorful and pretty. They drink the water. They look happy too.

Sam and Mia say, "Thank you, mister. You are very nice. You showed us something new. We are sorry we fought. We are friends again."

The man says, "You are welcome, children. I am glad you learned something. And I am glad you are friends. Friends should share and be fair. That is how you have fun." He smiles and waves. He turns off the tap. He takes his key and leaves.

They look around. They see a mail truck. It has a big box on the back. They have an idea.

"Maybe we can mail the bird to the zoo," Ben says. "The zoo can take care of the bird."

They run to the mail truck. They ask the mailman for help.

"Please, mister, can you help us?" Anna says. "There is a big bird on the fence. It is hurt. Can you mail it to the zoo?"

The mailman is surprised. He looks at the ostrich. He sees it is in pain. He feels sorry for the ostrich.

"OK, kids, I will help you," the mailman says. "But we have to be careful. The bird is delicate. We have to be gentle."

He gets a big blanket. He wraps the ostrich in the blanket. He lifts the ostrich off the fence. He puts the ostrich in the box. He closes the box. He writes "To the zoo" on the box.

"Thank you, mister, you are very kind," Anna and Ben say.

"You're welcome, kids, you are very brave," the mailman says. "Now, let's go to the zoo. The bird will be happy there."

They get in the mail truck. They drive to the zoo. They give the box to the zookeeper. The zookeeper opens the box. He sees the ostrich. He smiles.

"Hello, little ostrich, welcome to the zoo," the zookeeper says. "Don't worry, we will take good care of you."

The ostrich feels better. It sees other ostriches. It makes new friends.

Anna and Ben are happy. They wave goodbye to the ostrich.

"Bye, bird, we hope you like your new home," Anna and Ben say.

"Thank you, kids, you saved my life," the ostrich says.

The end.

"Where can we find some water?" Lily asked Tom.

Tom looked up at the sky. He saw some white clouds. He had an idea.

"Maybe we can drink from the clouds!" he said. "They look like water."

Lily nodded. She thought it was a good idea. They ran to the big hill and climbed to the top. They hoped they could reach the clouds.

But when they got to the top, they saw something strange. The clouds were not white anymore. They were red!

"What happened to the clouds?" Lily wondered.

Tom pointed to a big plane. The plane was flying in the sky and making red smoke. The smoke was coloring the clouds.

"That plane is making the clouds red!" he said. "It is not water. It is smoke."

Lily felt sad. She wanted to drink water, not smoke.

"Let's go back," she said. "Maybe we can find some water in the park."

Tom agreed. They went down the hill and ran back to the park. They saw a fountain with clear water. They were very happy.

They drank some water from the fountain. They felt cool and refreshed.

They smiled at each other and continued to play. They forgot about the red clouds.

Lily and Ben like to create things with their toys. They have many animals, cars, blocks and dolls. One day, they decide to create a zoo in their room. They put the animals in different places and make sounds for them.

"Look, this is the lion cage. Roar!" Lily says, holding a yellow toy lion.

"And this is the elephant area. Prrr!" Ben says, lifting a gray toy elephant with his trunk.

They have fun creating the zoo and pretending to be zookeepers. They feed the animals, clean their cages and talk to them.

But then, they hear a knock on the door. It is their mom. She opens the door and sees the mess in their room. She is not happy.

"What is this? What did you create?" she asks, looking at the toys everywhere.

"It's a zoo, mom. We made it with our toys. Do you like it?" Lily and Ben say, smiling.

"A zoo? It looks more like a mess. And some of these animals are very ugly. Look at this monkey. It has no tail and one eye. And this giraffe. It has spots of different colors and a short neck. Where did you get these toys?" mom says, picking up some of the animals.

"We made them, mom. We used scissors, glue and paint. We wanted to make them different and funny. We like them. They are our ugly animals." Lily and Ben say, proudly.

Mom sighs. She knows they are creative, but she also wants them to be tidy and careful. She tells them to clean up their room and put away their toys. She also tells them to be more careful with their scissors, glue and paint. She says they can keep their ugly animals, but they have to take good care of them.

Lily and Ben agree. They love their mom and their zoo. They clean up their room and put their animals in a box. They say goodbye to them and promise to play with them again soon. They hug their mom and say sorry for the mess. Mom hugs them back and says she loves them. She says they are very creative, but they also have to be responsible. She says she is proud of them. They smile and say thank you. They are happy.

Lily liked to record her voice with her toy phone. She would say funny things and then listen to them. She thought it was a smart game. She wanted to show her big brother Tom how she could record.

One morning, she saw Tom eating cereal in the kitchen. She had an idea. She sneaked behind him and pressed the record button on her phone. She said, "Tom is a silly monkey who likes to eat bananas." Then she ran away, giggling.

Tom heard her voice and turned around. He saw her phone on the table. He was angry. He did not like to be called a silly monkey. He grabbed her phone and chased after her. He wanted to make her say sorry.

Lily ran to her room and locked the door. She was scared. She did not want Tom to take her phone. She heard him banging on the door and shouting. She wished she had not recorded him.

Then she had another idea. She pressed the play button on her phone. She heard her voice again, saying, "Tom is a silly monkey who likes to eat bananas." She laughed. She thought it was funny. She opened the door and showed Tom her phone. She said, "Look, Tom, I recorded you. Do you want to hear it?"

Tom saw her smile and heard her voice. He was not angry anymore. He thought it was funny too. He laughed. He said, "OK, Lily, you are a smart girl who likes to record. But I am not a silly monkey who likes to eat bananas. I am a cool lion who likes to eat cereal. Can I record you too?"

Lily nodded. She said, "Yes, Tom, you can record me too. But only if you share your cereal with me."

Tom agreed. He said, "Deal. Come on, Lily, let's go to the kitchen and record and eat cereal together."

They went to the kitchen and played with the phone and ate cereal. They were happy. They were friends.

Lily was scared. She did not want the bird to hurt Ben. She cared for Ben. She ran after him and hugged him.

"I don't know. Maybe the bird likes the orange too. Maybe the bird thinks we are bad." Ben said.

They decided to leave the orange alone. They went to play with other things. They were still friends. They were happy.

"Oh no! What have I done?" Sam cries.

Tom hears the noise and goes outside. He sees his broken helicopter. He is very sad and angry.

"Sam, you broke my helicopter! You did not listen to me! You are a bad friend!" Tom shouts.

"I'm sorry, Tom. I did not mean to break it. I was having fun. Please forgive me," Sam says.

Tom thinks for a while. He remembers that Sam is his friend. He knows that Sam is sorry. He decides to forgive him.

"It's OK, Sam. I forgive you. But you have to be more careful next time. And you have to help me fix my helicopter," Tom says.

"Thank you, Tom. You are a good friend. I will help you fix it. And I will share my toys with you too," Sam says.

They hug and go inside. They look for glue and tape. They try to fix the helicopter. They learn to be careful and to share.

The end.

Jenny carried the leaf home and gently placed in a potted plant on her windowsill. From here, she could see the leaf and support it like a friend.

The leaf was happy to have Jenny's friendship and it felt loved and supported. Sometimes, when Jenny was feeling sad, she would look out her window and the leaf would make her feel better.

The leaf and Jenny lived happily together ever after.

The animals were surprised when they lifted the pot and something wonderful appeared! A large pile of candy emerged from the pot and the animals were overjoyed. They shared the candy amongst themselves and were so thankful.

From that day on, the foolish pot stayed in the forest and brought joy and surprises to the animals. They all had much fun together and it was a great adventure.

Once upon a time there was an intelligent frog. He was very clever and liked to explore the world around him. One day he hopped to a nearby pond and saw a leaf floating on the surface. Curious, he hopped onto the leaf and let the water drop him down the stream.

As he floated, he saw many other animals in the stream and soon felt he was in a great adventure. The wind blew the leaf and the frog was happy as he floated over the water. 

Suddenly, he saw something that made him want to jump off the leaf - a friendly duck was swimming towards him! The frog said hello and the two quickly became friends. The duck even promised to show the frog something amazing. 

The duck took the frog further down the stream and stopped at a waterfall. The frog was amazed. The water was rushing fast and the view was beautiful. 

The intelligent frog wanted to stay and explore, but the duck encouraged him to jump off the leaf and join the other frogs living in the pond. The frog trusted his new friend and made a big splash as he dropped into the pond. 

And so the intelligent frog began his exciting new life as a pond frog with many wonderful friends!

Once upon a time there was a sad little boy called Joe. He loved playing with his friends in the park but one day something bad happened. The ground started shaking and Joe felt scared. He wanted to escape but he couldn't move. Joe started to tear and felt so sad.

Just then he heard a loud noise coming from the sky and saw a big bird. It was an eagle! Joe had never seen an eagle before so he was excited. The eagle swooped down to pick Joe up and lifted him high above the ground. Joe felt safe with the eagle and he could escape the shaking ground.

They flew high in the sky for what seemed like hours. Joe finally felt safe and happy again. He waved goodbye to the eagle and thanked it for helping him escape. Joe never forgot the special adventure he had with the eagle!

On her way home, Lucy saw a hungry bunny. The bunny looked sad. Lucy thought she could fill the bunny's tummy with the perfect apple. She gave the apple to the bunny. The bunny ate it and was very happy. Lucy felt good about helping the bunny, even if she didn't have the perfect apple anymore.

Tim was brave and helped the tornado go away. His friends were all safe and happy. They thanked Tim for being so polite and helpful. From that day on, they all lived happily ever after.

Now Lily could go outside and play in the snow without feeling cold. Her mom allowed her to stay outside for as long as she wanted, as long as she wore her new coat. Lily was so happy and grateful for her new coat. She could enjoy the snow and make snowmen again!

Once upon a time, there was a big mountain with fire inside. It was called a volcano. One day, a little boy and his mom went to see the volcano. They climbed up and up until they reached the top. The boy looked down and felt dizzy. 

Suddenly, the volcano started to shake and make loud noises. The boy's mom told him to raise his arms up high and hold on tight. They watched as the volcano erupted and hot lava came shooting out. The boy was scared but also amazed at the same time. 

After the volcano stopped erupting, the boy and his mom went back down the mountain. The boy was happy they got to see the volcano, but also happy to be back on solid ground. He told his friends all about the big mountain and how it made him feel dizzy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a very delicate glass cup that she loved to drink juice from. One day, Lily accidentally dropped the glass and it broke into many pieces. She was very sad and didn't know what to do.

Her mom saw her crying and asked what happened. Lily told her about the broken glass cup. Her mom hugged her and said, "It's okay, Lily. Sometimes things break and we can't fix them. We just have to surrender to what has happened and move on."

Lily didn't understand what "surrender" meant, but she knew her mom was trying to help her feel better. They cleaned up the broken glass together and her mom promised to get her a new cup. Lily felt happy again knowing that her mom was there to help her.

After a week, Hoppy's leg felt better. He started to hop again, little by little. Soon, Hoppy was hopping all over the place, just like before. Hoppy was very happy and his friends were happy too. And they all hopped together, every day.

Tim's mom and dad thanked him for helping. They put the refrigerator in its place, and then they all picked up the toys together. Tim was happy that he could help, and they all had fun playing with the toys after.

So, the duck and the ugly frog played together all day. They had so much fun. The frog's look changed and he became happy. In the end, the duck and the frog became best friends.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there lived a loyal dog named Buddy. Buddy loved to play with his ball. He would throw it up in the air and catch it with his mouth. Buddy's best friend was a little girl named Anna. They played together every day.

One day, while Anna and Buddy were playing, the ball rolled into the street. Buddy ran after it, but Anna knew that was trouble. She shouted, "Buddy, stop!" Buddy stopped and looked at Anna. He knew he should listen to her.

Anna walked over to Buddy and picked up the ball. She said, "We have to be careful, Buddy. The street can be dangerous." Buddy wagged his tail, happy that Anna was looking out for him. From that day on, they made sure to only play in the yard, away from the street. And they lived happily ever after, always staying loyal to each other.

Suddenly, Tim's gum fell out of his mouth and got stuck on his shoe. Tim started to panic. "Oh no! My gum is on my shoe!" he cried. Sue helped Tim get the gum off his shoe. They both laughed and played together in the park until the sun went down.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there was a lazy bird named Lulu. Lulu had many pretty feathers, but she did not like to fly. She loved to sit in her nest all day and look at her feathers.

One day, a little girl named Amy came to the forest. She saw Lulu sitting in her nest and said, "Hello, pretty bird! Can I touch your feather?" Lulu thought for a moment and then said, "Yes, you can touch my feather, but please be gentle."

Amy reached up and gently touched Lulu's feather. It was very soft. "Thank you for letting me touch your feather," Amy said. "I have never met such a lazy bird before! Do you not like to fly?"

Lulu looked at Amy and said, "I do like to fly, but I am scared. What if I fall?" Amy smiled and said, "If you never try, you will never know. I will be here to catch you if you fall. I promise."

Lulu took a deep breath and decided to permit herself to try. She jumped out of her nest and began to fly. She was so happy that she had tried. From that day on, Lulu was no longer a lazy bird. She flew all over the forest, making new friends and having fun. And she always remembered the little girl who had helped her learn to fly.

But then, their mom came down to the basement. She saw the box and the sign. She was not happy. "What are you doing?" she asked. "You are making a mess and wasting paper. This is not an elevator. This is a fake."

Lily and Max felt sad. They did not want to make their mom angry. They tried to explain. "We are playing pretend, mom. We are using our imagination. We are not hurting anyone."

Their mom listened. She understood. She smiled. "I'm sorry, kids. I was too harsh. Playing pretend is good. It helps you learn and have fun. But you also need to be careful and respectful. You can't use things without asking. You can't leave a mess. You can't lie. Do you understand?"

Lily and Max nodded. They said sorry. They hugged their mom. They cleaned up the box and the paper. They learned a lesson. Playing pretend is good, but being honest and responsible is better.

Tom and Lily like to play number games. They have cards with numbers on them. They take turns to pick a card and say the number. If they say the right number, they get a point. If they say the wrong number, they lose a point.

One day, Tom has a clever idea. He picks a card and says, "This is number ten." But he shows Lily a card with number five. Lily thinks Tom is wrong and says, "No, that is number five. You lose a point."

Tom smiles and says, "No, Lily, look again. This is number ten." He turns the card upside down and shows Lily. Now the card looks like number ten. Lily is surprised and says, "Wow, Tom, you are very clever. How did you do that?"

Tom says, "It is easy. Some numbers look the same when you turn them upside down. Like six and nine, or one and one. Do you want to try?"

Lily says, "Yes, I want to try. This is fun." She picks a card and says, "This is number eight." She shows Tom a card with number three. Tom knows Lily's trick and says, "No, Lily, that is number three. You lose a point."

Lily says, "No, Tom, look again. This is number eight." She turns the card sideways and shows Tom. Now the card looks like number eight. Tom is amazed and says, "Wow, Lily, you are very clever too. How did you do that?"

Lily says, "It is easy. Some numbers look the same when you turn them sideways. Like three and eight, or zero and zero. Do you want to play more?"

Tom says, "Yes, I want to play more. This is fun." They play more number games and have a lot of fun. They are both very clever and learn new things.

One day, an adventurous penguin named Pippa wanted to explore the big ice land. She said to her mama, "Mama, can I go and see what is over there?" She pointed to a hill far away.

Her mama said, "No, Pippa, it is too dangerous. You might get lost or meet a scary animal. You should stay with me and the other penguins."

But Pippa did not listen. She ignored her mama and sneaked away when she was not looking. She waddled and slid on the ice, feeling happy and curious. She saw many new things, like shiny rocks, fluffy snowflakes and colorful fish.

Soon, she reached the hill and climbed up. She wanted to see what was on the other side. But when she got to the top, she saw something that made her very afraid. It was a big, furry, growling bear! The bear saw her too and started to run towards her.

Pippa was so scared that she forgot how to move. She wished she had listened to her mama. She closed her eyes and hoped the bear would go away. But then, she heard a loud honk and felt a warm wing around her. It was her mama! Her mama had followed her and scared the bear away. She hugged Pippa and said, "Pippa, I am so glad you are safe. But you should never ignore me again. I only want to protect you and love you."

Pippa felt sorry and ashamed. She said, "I am sorry, mama. I was wrong. I wanted to be adventurous, but I did not think of the danger. I love you too, mama. Can we go home now?"

Her mama smiled and said, "Yes, Pippa, we can go home. But first, let me show you something. Look over there." She pointed to the other side of the hill, where the sun was setting and making the ice sparkle. "This is a beautiful sight, but it is not worth risking your life. You can be adventurous, but you also need to be careful and listen to me. Do you understand?"

Pippa nodded and said, "I understand, mama. Thank you for saving me and showing me this. You are the best mama in the world."

They cuddled and watched the sun go down. Then, they slid and waddled back to their home, where the other penguins welcomed them. Pippa learned her lesson and never ignored her mama again. She still liked to explore, but she always asked her mama first and stayed close to her. She was happy and safe, and so was her mama.

Sam and Tom were brothers who liked to sail. They had a small boat that they took to the lake. They sailed fast and slow, left and right, and had fun.

One day, they saw a big field of wheat near the lake. The wheat was yellow and tall and looked soft. Sam wanted to touch the wheat. He said to Tom, "Let's go to the wheat and play."

Tom said, "No, Sam. The wheat is not ours. It belongs to the farmer. He works hard to grow the wheat. He will be angry if we mess it up."

But Sam did not listen. He jumped out of the boat and ran to the wheat. He pushed the wheat with his hands and feet. He made a path in the wheat. He laughed and shouted, "This is fun!"

Tom stayed in the boat. He was scared and sad. He saw the farmer coming from his house. The farmer had a big hat and a big stick. He looked angry. He saw Sam in the wheat. He yelled, "Hey, you! Get out of my wheat! You are ruining my crop!"

Sam heard the farmer and was scared too. He tried to run back to the boat, but he got lost in the wheat. He could not see Tom or the lake. He cried, "Help! Help!"

Tom heard Sam and was brave. He got out of the boat and went to the wheat. He followed Sam's path and found him. He said, "Sam, I'm here. Come with me. We have to say sorry to the farmer."

Sam and Tom came out of the wheat and saw the farmer. He was still angry, but he saw that they were just children. He said, "Why did you do this? Do you know how much work and money it takes to grow wheat? Do you know how many people need wheat to eat bread and cake and pasta?"

Sam and Tom felt bad. They said, "We're sorry, sir. We didn't know. We just wanted to play. We won't do it again."

The farmer sighed. He said, "Well, I'm glad you're sorry. But you have to learn to respect other people's things. Wheat is not a toy. It is a food. You should be grateful for the wheat and the farmer who grows it."

Sam and Tom nodded. They said, "We're sorry, sir. We're grateful for the wheat and for you. Can we do anything to help you fix the wheat?"

The farmer smiled. He said, "That's very kind of you. You can help me by picking up some of the wheat that you knocked down and putting it in this basket. Sam and Tom smiled too. They said, "That sounds good, sir. We're sorry, sir. We're grateful, sir. We'll do it, sir."

And they did. They helped the farmer, the miller, the baker, and the people. They learned a lot about wheat and how it makes food. They also learned to be careful, respectful, and grateful. They never played in the wheat again. They still liked to sail, but they also liked to help. They were good brothers and good friends.

Tim was happy to display his waffle to Sam. They both sat down and ate the waffle together. The deep brown waffle was the best waffle they ever had. They laughed and played all day.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a big church. Many people went there to sing and be happy. One day, a little boy named Tim saw smoke coming from the church. He knew something was wrong.

Tim ran to the church and saw that it was starting to burn. He was scared, but he wanted to be helpful. He remembered that water could stop the fire. So, he ran to the river and filled a bucket with water. Then, he ran back to the church and threw the water on the fire.

Tim did this many times. Soon, other people saw what Tim was doing and they came to help too. Together, they all put out the fire and saved the church. Everyone in the town was so proud of helpful Tim. From that day on, Tim was known as the brave boy who saved the church.

Once upon a time, there was a man with a big mustache. He was very strong. His mustache was so big that everyone in the town knew him. They called him "Strong Mustache Man."

One day, Strong Mustache Man saw a big rock in the road. People could not walk or play because of the rock. Strong Mustache Man wanted to help. He put his hands on the rock and started to push. He pushed and pushed with all his strength.

As he pushed, the people in the town watched. They clapped and cheered for Strong Mustache Man. With one last big push, the rock moved out of the way. The people were happy and thanked Strong Mustache Man. From that day on, everyone knew that Strong Mustache Man was not just strong, but also kind and helpful.

Once upon a time, there was a jolly boy named Tom. He liked to play with his red ball in the big park near his home. One sunny day, Tom went to the park to play with his ball.

As Tom was playing, his ball went far away into the bushes. He went to look for it and found a magic stick. Tom picked up the magic stick and said, "I wish my ball would disappear!" Suddenly, his ball was gone!

Tom was sad and said, "Oh no, I want my ball back!" A nice lady heard him and said, "You have a magic stick, just say you want your ball back." Tom said, "I wish my ball would come back!" And just like that, his red ball came back. Tom was so happy and played with his ball all day long.

Once upon a time, there was a weak cricket named Tim. Tim lived in a big green field with his family. All the other crickets were strong and could jump very high. Tim was sad because he could not jump as high as the others.

One day, Tim met a wise old frog. The frog said he could supply Tim with a special drink that would make him strong. Tim was very happy and drank the special drink. He started to feel stronger and could jump higher than before.

But soon, Tim felt sick. He jumped too high and fell down. He was hurt and could not move. The wise old frog told Tim that he should have been happy with who he was. The moral of the story is to be happy with what you have and not try to change just to fit in.

But the pony does not like Lily. It does not want to be touched by a stranger. It is scared and angry. It kicks its legs and shakes its head. It makes a loud noise. It yells, "Neigh! Neigh! Go away!"

Lily is surprised and sad. She does not understand why the pony yells at her. She starts to cry. She runs back to her mom and dad. They hug her and comfort her. They say, "It's okay, Lily. The pony is not mean. It is just shy and nervous. It does not know you. You have to be gentle and careful with animals. They have feelings too."

Lily nods and wipes her tears. She says, "I'm sorry, pony. I just wanted to play with you. Maybe next time you will let me." She looks at the pony from a distance. She hopes that one day, the pony will be her friend. She smiles and hugs her toy pony. She says, "You are still my favorite pony. You are so flexible and nice."

Sara and Ben were twins who liked to walk in the park with their mom. One day, they saw a big pile of white powder on the grass. It looked like snow, but it was not cold.

"Can we play with the powder, mom?" Sara asked.

"No, my loves, that is not snow. That is soap powder. Someone spilled it by mistake. It is not good for you or the plants. We should leave it alone," mom said.

But Ben was curious. He wanted to touch the powder and see what it felt like. He sneaked away from mom and Sara and ran to the pile. He grabbed a handful of powder and threw it in the air. It made a lovely cloud of white.

"Wow, this is fun!" Ben said. He did not see the dog that was coming towards him.

The dog was big and brown and liked to chase things. He saw the white cloud and thought it was a bird. He ran after it and jumped on Ben. He knocked him down and licked his face. He also got some powder in his mouth and nose. He did not like it. He started to cough and sneeze.

"Help, mom, help!" Ben cried. He was scared and dirty.

Mom heard Ben and ran to him. She saw the dog and the powder and understood what happened. She shooed the dog away and picked up Ben. She hugged him and checked if he was hurt.

"Are you okay, Ben?" mom asked.

"I'm sorry, mom. I was naughty. I did not listen to you. I wanted to play with the powder. But it was not fun. It was bad. The dog was scary. And the powder was yucky. It made me and the dog sick," Ben said.

Mom was not angry. She was glad that Ben was safe. She also felt sorry for the dog. She took Ben to a fountain and washed his face and hands. She also gave him some water to drink.

"It's okay, Ben. I forgive you. But you have to learn to obey me. I know what is good for you and what is not. The powder was not for playing. It was for washing clothes. It can hurt you and the animals and the plants. You have to be careful and respectful of nature. Do you understand?" mom said.

"Yes, mom. I understand. I'm sorry. I love you," Ben said.

"I love you too, Ben. And I love you, Sara. Come on, let's go home. We have some lovely cookies waiting for us," mom said.

Sara had been watching the whole thing. She was glad that Ben was okay. She also learned a lesson. She did not want to play with the powder. She wanted to play with mom and Ben and the cookies. She hugged them and they walked home together. They were happy.

Sam and Ben are brothers. They like to play catch with a ball. One day, they play catch in the house. They are careless. They do not see the office where Dad works.

Dad is busy. He writes on his computer. He does not hear Sam and Ben. The ball flies into the office. It hits Dad's computer. The computer makes a loud noise. It stops working.

Dad is angry. He comes out of the office. He sees Sam and Ben. He says, "What did you do? You broke my computer! You are careless! You should not play catch in the house!"

Sam and Ben are scared. They say, "We are sorry, Dad. We did not mean to break your computer. We just wanted to play catch. We did not see your office."

Dad is still angry. He says, "You should see where you throw the ball. You should be careful. You should play catch outside. Now I have to fix my computer. Go to your room. No more catch for today."

Sam and Ben are sad. They go to their room. They do not play catch. They wish they were more careful. They hope Dad can fix his computer. They hope Dad is not angry for long.

Ben has a new jacket with a zipper. He likes to zip it up and down. Zip, zip, zip. He thinks it is fun. He wants to show his jacket to his friend Sam.

He goes to Sam's house and knocks on the door. Sam's mom opens the door. She is bald. She has no hair on her head. Ben is surprised. He has never seen a bald person before. He wonders why she is bald.

"Hello, Ben. Sam is in his room. You can go and play with him," Sam's mom says. She smiles at Ben. She is very nice.

Ben goes to Sam's room. He sees Sam playing with his toys. He says hello to Sam. He shows him his jacket with the zipper. Sam likes it too. He zips it up and down. Zip, zip, zip. They think it is fun.

They play with the toys and the jacket. They have a good time. The sun shines through the window. It makes Sam's mom's head shine too. She looks like a star. Ben thinks she is pretty. He is not surprised anymore. He likes Sam's mom. He gives her a hug. She hugs him back. She is happy.

Anna and Ben are playing in their room. They have many toys, but they like to make their own games. They find a long scarf and a big box. They have an idea.

"Let's play hide and seek!" says Anna. "You can hide in the box and I will find you."

"OK!" says Ben. He gets in the box and pulls the scarf over it. He waits for Anna to count.

Anna counts to ten. She looks around the room. She sees the box with the scarf. She thinks Ben is hiding there. She walks to the box and says, "I found you!"

But when she lifts the scarf, she sees nothing. The box is empty. She is surprised. She blinks her eyes. Where is Ben?

She hears a giggle behind her. She turns around and sees Ben. He is hiding behind the wall. He jumps out and says, "Boo!"

Anna laughs. She says, "You tricked me! You are very clever!"

Ben smiles. He says, "You are very fun! Let's play again!"

They hug and play some more. They are happy.

Tom and Sue were friends who liked to play with boats. They had many boats of different colors and sizes. They would sail them in the pond near their house. They had fun watching the boats go fast or slow, turn or spin, float or sink.

One day, Tom found a big boat in his garage. It was red and shiny, with a white sail and a flag. He was very happy and wanted to show it to Sue. He ran to her house and knocked on the door.

"Look, Sue, look what I have!" he said, holding the boat.

"Wow, Tom, that is a nice boat!" Sue said. "Can I see it?"

"Sure, but be careful. It is very value. My dad gave it to me for my birthday. He said it was his when he was little. He said it can sail very far and fast."

"Can we sail it in the pond?" Sue asked.

"Okay, but only for a little bit. I don't want it to get dirty or wet," Tom said.

They went to the pond and put the boat in the water. They watched it sail away from them, faster and faster. It looked like a red dot on the blue pond.

"Wow, it is so fast!" Sue said.

"Yes, it is. But how do we get it back?" Tom said.

They tried to call the boat, but it did not listen. They tried to throw stones at it, but they missed. They tried to swim after it, but they were too slow.

They started to cry. They lost the value boat. They were sad and angry.

"Why did you let go of the boat, Tom?" Sue said.

"I didn't, Sue. It just sailed away. It was too fast," Tom said.

"It is your fault, Tom. You should have been more careful. You are a bad friend," Sue said.

"No, Sue, you are a bad friend. You wanted to sail the boat too. You are sour," Tom said.

They stopped talking to each other. They went back to their houses, still crying.

The next day, they saw a man walking to the pond. He had a big smile and a red boat in his hands. It was Tom's boat. He had found it on the other side of the pond. He saw Tom and Sue and waved at them.

"Hello, kids. Is this your boat?" he said.

"Yes, yes, it is!" Tom and Sue said. They ran to the man and hugged the boat.

"Thank you, thank you, mister!" they said.

"You're welcome, kids. I'm glad I found it. It is a very nice boat. It reminds me of my childhood. I used to sail boats like this with my friends. We had a lot of fun," the man said.

"Really? Did you ever lose your boats?" Tom asked.

"Sometimes, yes. But we always found them again. Or we made new ones. The important thing is to enjoy sailing and playing with your friends. That is the real value of a boat," the man said.

Tom and Sue looked at each other. They felt sorry for what they said yesterday. They realized they were silly and mean. They smiled and said sorry.

"Sorry, Tom. You are not a bad friend. You are a good friend," Sue said.

"Sorry, Sue. You are not sour. You are sweet," Tom said.

They hugged and said they were still friends. They thanked the man again and asked him if he wanted to sail with them. He said yes and they all went to the pond. They sailed the red boat and their other boats. They had fun and laughed. They learned a lesson. They learned to value their boats and their friends.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play with toys. One day, they find a big box. The box has many furry animals inside. Lily and Ben are happy.

Lily picks up a furry cat. She says, "This is my cat. I love cats. They are soft and nice."

Ben picks up a furry dog. He says, "This is my dog. I love dogs. They are fun and loyal."

Lily and Ben look at each other. They disagree. They say, "No, my animal is better. Your animal is not good."

They start to argue. They raise their voices. They pull each other's animals. They are not happy.

Mom hears them. She comes to the box. She says, "Stop, Lily and Ben. Why are you fighting? You both have furry animals. They are all good. You can share them. You can play together."

Lily and Ben stop. They think. They use their brains. They say, "You are right, Mom. We are sorry. We can share. We can play together."

They hug Mom. They hug each other. They hug their furry animals. They are happy. They are friends.

Tim and Lily were playing in the park. They saw a big hill with a hole in it. They wanted to see what was inside.

"Let's go in the hole," Tim said.

"OK," Lily said.

They crawled into the hole. It was dark and cold. They used a flashlight to look around. They saw a lot of bones. They were scared.

"Are these bones from animals?" Lily asked.

"I don't know," Tim said.

They saw a big bone that looked like a head. It had two holes for eyes and a hole for a mouth. It was a skeleton.

"Ah!" Tim and Lily screamed.

They ran out of the hole. They saw a man sitting on a bench. He had a big hat and a long coat. He was reading a book.

"Help! Help!" Tim and Lily shouted.

The man did not look at them. He did not hear them. He was deaf.

Tim and Lily ran to their mom. She was waiting for them near the swings.

"Mom, mom, we saw a skeleton in the hole!" Tim and Lily said.

"A skeleton?" Mom asked.

"Yes, a skeleton! It was scary!" Tim and Lily said.

Mom hugged them. She smiled.

"Maybe it was a dinosaur skeleton," she said.

"A dinosaur?" Tim and Lily asked.

"Yes, a dinosaur. They lived a long time ago. They had big bones. Some of them were friendly and some of them were not," Mom said.

"Wow," Tim and Lily said.

They looked at the hole. They wondered if the skeleton was a friendly dinosaur or not.

They shrugged. They did not know.

"Look, Ben, a jellyfish!" Lila pointed to a pink blob on the sand. "It's so pretty and shiny. Can we touch it?"

"No, Lila, we can't touch it. It can hurt us with its stings. Mom said so." Ben shook his head. "We should leave it alone. Maybe the waves will send it back to the sea."

"But I want to see it closer. Maybe it's friendly. Maybe it's lonely." Lila moved closer to the jellyfish. "Hi, jellyfish. Do you want to play with us?"

The jellyfish didn't answer. It didn't move. It didn't seem to care about Lila and Ben. It was very independent. It didn't need anyone to play with. It was happy in its own way.

Lila felt sad. She wanted to make a new friend. She reached out her hand to touch the jellyfish. But Ben grabbed her arm and pulled her back.

"Ow, Ben, that hurts. Let me go!" Lila cried.

"Lila, no. Trust me. The jellyfish is not a good friend. It can make you sick. Come on, let's go play with something else." Ben said.

One day, a dog and a cat were playing in the park. They saw a big ball that was red and shiny. They both wanted the ball, so they ran to get it. But they got there at the same time, and they started to fight. They pulled and pushed and bit and scratched, but neither of them could get the ball.

A bird was watching them from a tree. He thought they were very funny, because they were making a lot of noise and making silly faces. He flew down and said, "Why are you fighting over the ball? It is not yours, and it is not fun to hurt each other. Why don't you share the ball and play together?"

The dog and the cat stopped fighting and looked at the bird. They felt ashamed, because they knew he was right. They said, "We are sorry, bird. You are very smart. How can we share the ball and play together?"

The bird said, "It is easy. You can take turns with the ball. One of you can roll the ball, and the other can chase it. Then you can switch. That way, you both can have fun with the ball, and you can be friends."

The dog and the cat liked the bird's idea. They thanked him and said, "You are very kind, bird. You helped us solve our problem. Do you want to play with us?"

The bird said, "Yes, I would love to play with you. You are very nice, dog and cat. You learned to share and be friends. That is the best way to have fun."

The end.

Moral: Sharing is caring, and friendship is fun.

Mia and Ben were playing in the kitchen. They liked to pretend they were chefs and make yummy food. They used pots and pans, spoons and forks, and some things from the fridge.

"Look, I made a cake!" Mia said, holding a plate with a slice of bread and some cream on top. "Do you want some?"

"Yes, please!" Ben said, taking a bite. "It is very good. Can I have more cream?"

"Sure!" Mia said, opening the fridge. She saw a big bottle of cream and took it out. She tried to squeeze some cream on Ben's plate, but the bottle was too hard. She pushed and pushed, but nothing came out.

"Let me help you," Ben said, grabbing the bottle. He pushed and pushed, too, but still nothing came out. He pushed harder and harder, until...

POP!

The bottle exploded and cream flew everywhere. It landed on the table, the floor, the walls, and the children. Mia and Ben were covered in white sticky cream. They looked at each other and started to laugh.

"Oh no!" they heard a voice say. It was Mom, who had just come home from work. She saw the mess in the kitchen and frowned. "What happened here? This is not tidy at all!"

"Sorry, Mom," Mia and Ben said together. "We were playing chefs and the cream bottle popped."

Mom sighed and shook her head. "Well, I'm glad you had fun, but you need to clean up this mess. Go wash your hands and faces, and then help me wipe the cream off everything. And next time, please be more careful with the cream. It is not a toy, it is for eating."

"Okay, Mom," Mia and Ben said. They ran to the bathroom and washed the cream off. Then they came back and helped Mom clean the kitchen. They used cloths and water and soap, and soon the kitchen was tidy again.

"Thank you, Mia and Ben," Mom said, smiling. "You did a good job. Now, how about we have some real cake for dessert? I bought one from the bakery. It has cream on it, too, but it will not pop, I promise."

"Yay!" Mia and Ben said, clapping their hands. They followed Mom to the dining room, where a delicious cake was waiting for them. They cut some slices and ate them happily. They liked the cream on the cake, but they liked Mom more. They gave her a big hug and a kiss, and said, "We love you, Mom."

"I love you, too, Mia and Ben," Mom said, hugging them back. "You are my sweet cream pies."

Tom and Sam are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big jar of money on a bench. The jar has a sign that says "For the poor".

"Wow, look at all that money!" Tom says. "I wish I had some."

"Me too," Sam says. "Do you think anyone is watching?"

Tom looks around. He does not see anyone. He has an idea. He says to Sam, "I dare you to take some money from the jar. Just a little bit. No one will know."

Sam feels scared. He knows it is wrong to take money that is not his. He says to Tom, "No, I don't want to. That is not honest. The money is for the poor. They need it more than us."

Tom laughs. He says, "You are a chicken. I am not afraid. I will take some money. Watch me." He runs to the jar and grabs a handful of money. He puts it in his pocket.

Suddenly, a man comes out of a shop. He sees Tom with the money. He is angry. He says, "Hey, you! What are you doing? That is my money! I was collecting it for the poor. Give it back!"

Tom is scared. He drops the money and runs away. He does not look at Sam. He feels bad.

Sam is sad. He does not want to be friends with Tom anymore. He thinks Tom is not honest. He goes to the man and says, "I am sorry. Tom dared me to take some money, but I did not. I know it is wrong. Here, take this money. It is yours."

The man smiles. He says, "Thank you, young man. You are very honest. You did the right thing. Here, take this candy. It is for you."

Sam takes the candy. He says, "Thank you, sir. You are very kind. I hope the poor get the money."

The man says, "They will. And I hope you find a better friend than Tom."

Sam nods. He walks away. He feels good. He thinks, "I am glad I did not dare to take the money. It is better to be honest."

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved cars and trucks, but he had a problem. His toy car was broken and he didn't know how to fix it. He asked his mom for help, but she didn't know how to solve the problem either.

One day, Timmy was playing outside when he saw his neighbor driving a big vehicle. It was a brilliant red truck! Timmy ran over to the neighbor and asked if he could help fix his toy car. The neighbor was happy to help and together they solved the problem.

Timmy was so happy that his toy car was fixed and he could play with it again. He thanked his neighbor for being so kind and brilliant. From that day on, Timmy made sure to take care of his toy car so it wouldn't break again.
